Define $$D_{\\{i,j\\}}(H)=\\int_H X_j(t-)v_i(t)\n       \\sum_\\zeta r_{i,\\zeta}(b_{i,\\zeta}-1)(\\zeta-t_i)\\,dt\n       +\\int_H X_i(t-)v_j(t)\n       \\sum_\\zeta r_{j,\\zeta}(b_{j,\\zeta}-1)(\\zeta-t_j)\\,dt .$$ With arbitrarily high inverse-polynomial probability, using the joint boundary-and-interior convention for a bridge portion, $$\\label{score:one-insertion-bounds}\n |D(H)|_2\\lesssim_\\beta d^{1/4}\\sqrt{\\mathcal J_H/n},\\qquad\n |D(H)|_4\\lesssim_\\beta d^{5/16}n^{-1/4}\\sqrt{\\mathcal J_H}.$$ For an insertion of order $h>1$, or with bounded predictable weights that may depend on $e$, the same bounds with $d^{1/2}$ in place of $d^{1/4}$ and $d^{5/16}$ hold without using overlap estimates.         "exact_quote": "Fix an admissible oriented law $\\mathsf Q$, its oriented filtration, and any permitted auxiliary-data augmentation.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-clock-scores",
        "exact_quote": "*(i) Conditional coefficients.* For every deterministic matrix on <a href=\"#hist:static-conditions\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"hist:static-conditions\">[hist:static-conditions]</a>, every tested path law, and every node $I$ of length $D$ in its checked roots, the vectors in <a href=\"#score:R-definition\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"score:R-definition\">[score:R-definition]</a> satisfy, with arbitrarily high inverse-polynomial probability over their boundary states, $$\\label{score:R-basic}\n |R_l(I)|_\\infty\\lesssim_\\beta D^{l/2},\\qquad\n |R_l(I)|_2\\lesssim_\\beta D^{l/2-1},\\qquad\n |R_l(I)|_4\\lesssim_\\beta D^{l/2-1/2},\\qquad 1\\le l\\le K.$$ Also, $$\\label{score:R-l1}\n |R_3(I)|_1\\lesssim_\\beta D^{-1/4},\\qquad\n |R_l(I)|_1\\lesssim_\\beta D^{(l-4)/2},\\quad 4\\le l\\le K.$$ If $D\\ge Tn^{-0.005}$, the $L^4$ bound for $R_1$ has the additional factor $n^{-0.01}$, the $L^2$ bounds for $R_2,R_3$ have the additional factor $n^{-0.001}$, and the $L^1$ bound for $R_4$ has the additional factor $n^{-0.0007}$. The conclusions hold simultaneously for any polynomial collection of specified nodes and any fixed number of conditional copies, with the same exceptional-set convention.*\n\n\n\n**(ii) Raw representations.* Fix an admissible oriented law, its oriented filtration, and any permitted auxiliary-data augmentation, as in Lemma <a href=\"#score:raw-projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"score:raw-projection\">44</a>. Then fix a dyadic subtree $H$ of length $d$ in that portion and an order $1\\le l\\le K$. The following representations satisfy <a href=\"#score:raw-representation\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"score:raw-representation\">[score:raw-representation]</a> for every earlier vector $A$ in that lemma’s class, with the representation chosen from this fixed setup before $A$. If $l\\ge2$ and $d\\ge Tn^{-0.02}$, there is a representation for which $$\\label{score:raw-improvement}\n \\sum_\\alpha|V_\\alpha^{(l)}(H)|_2\n       \\lesssim_\\beta n^{-0.004}\n                   d^{(l-1)/2+1/4}\\sqrt{\\mathcal J_H/n}.$$ For every $1\\le l\\le K$, there is a representation for which $$\\label{score:raw-l1-projection}\n \\sum_\\alpha|V_\\alpha^{(l)}(H)|_1\n       \\lesssim_\\beta \\max\\{\\sqrt d,d^{l/2-5/4}\\}\\sqrt{\\mathcal J_H/n}.$$ For $l=4$ and $d\\ge Tn^{-0.006}$, the latter estimate has the additional factor $n^{-0.001}$. The two families here may differ from each other and from the family giving the two basic bounds in Lemma <a href=\"#score:raw-projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"score:raw-projection\">44</a>. These pathwise norm estimates have arbitrarily high inverse-polynomial probability with that lemma’s scope: for a bridge portion the probability is under the tested boundary law followed by the conditional interior. They are not uniform conditional assertions at every fixed boundary pair.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-universality",
        "exact_quote": "For the Rademacher coupling law, $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Law}}_{\\mathrm{Rad}}\\bigl(A_{n,J},B_{n,J}\\bigr)\n \\Longrightarrow\\mathop{\\mathrm{Law}}_g\\bigl(A_g,B_g\\bigr)$$ in $C_{\\mathrm{loc}}((0,\\infty))\\times\nC_{\\mathrm{loc}}((0,\\infty)^2)$, where $(A_g,B_g)$ is the Gaussian limit obtained by combining Proposition <a href=\"#prop:gaussian-subsequence\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:gaussian-subsequence\">25</a> with the identification of the entrance family in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:entrance-selection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:entrance-selection\">27</a>.         "exact_quote": "There are constants $a>0$ and $C_K<\\infty$ with the following property for all sufficiently small fixed $\\beta>0$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **heat-bath semigroup** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Write $P_t^J$ for this heat-bath semigroup.
- **critical time unit** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Let $\nu_n$ be the uniform law on the cube, independent of $J$, and set $T_n=n^{2/3}$.
- **waiting time and lag** ([source](#pm-h-3)): The variable $s$ is the waiting time after the quench and $t$ is the subsequent lag.
- **cylinder gradient form** ([source](#pm-h-3)): The cylinder gradient form $$\mathcal E_g(F)=\int\sum_{a\ge1}\|\partial_aF\|^2\,\,\mathrm d\Pi_g$$ is closable.
- **measurable density family** ([source](#pm-h-3)): We call a family $h_s^g\in L^2(\Pi_g)$ measurable when $(g,s)\mapsto\Pi_g[h_s^g\phi]$ is measurable for each test $\phi\in\mathcal{V}$.
- **locally uniform function space** ([source](#pm-h-3)): For an open set $V\subset\mathbb R^d$, $C_{\mathrm{loc}}(V)$ denotes the space of continuous functions with uniform convergence on every compact subset.
- **entropy dissipation functional** ([source](#pm-h-7)): We write $\mathcal E(f)=\mathcal E(f,f)$ and, for $z\ge0$, $\mathcal I(z)=\mathcal E(z,\log z)$, with its extended nonnegative value at zeros.
- **tight lower threshold** ([source](#pm-h-9)): A tight lower threshold for the dimension parameter $k_p=np^3$ has the same meaning with a deterministic threshold $K_\chi$ on each event.
- **relative entropy convention** ([source](#sec:warming)): For a probability $\nu\ll\pi$, let $D(\nu\Vert\pi)=\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\pi(\,\mathrm d\nu/\,\mathrm d\pi)$, and set this relative entropy to $+\infty$ otherwise.
- **positive logarithm** ([source](#sec:warming)): We use $\log_+z=\max\{\log z,0\}$ for $z>0$, with $z(\log_+z)^m=0$ at $z=0$.
- **tested path law** ([source](#stmt-hist-tested-law)): A checked history is one of the following subprobabilities, with initial probability either $\mu$ or the uniform cube probability:

| q-edge-growth | shifted limiting edge coordinate $g_i+b$ | ≤ | $C_{g,b}(1+i)^{2/3}$ | all indices i |
| q-entropy-warming | relative entropy of the evolved density | ≤ | $C(1+s^{-1.54})$ | every initial law, all positive rescaled times |
| q-kernel-warming | supremum of the heat kernel relative to the Gibbs measure | ≤ | $C\exp(C s^{-1.54})$ | times above a vanishing threshold |
| q-entropy-dissipation-exponent | scaled modified dissipation of a density | ≥ | $c\,\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\mu(z)^{1.662}$ | entropy above a threshold |
| q-taylor-order | maximal Taylor order $K$ | = | $24$ | derivative orders |
| q-fourth-derivative-average | averaged fourth derivative of the localized observable | ≤ | $n^{-a_0}$ | edges |

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-spectral-edge** [claim](#stmt-edge-spectral) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-spectral): Resolvent transforms from an eigenvalue-only event, compactness and Stieltjes uniqueness. -> edge spectral limits and trace constants
- **step-saddle-density** [claim](#stmt-edge-norm-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-norm-density): Monotone saddle equation and Fourier inversion for Gaussian quadratic forms. -> saddle bounds and norm density
- **step-spherical-tails** [claim](#stmt-edge-spherical-tails) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-spherical-tails): Exponential Markov with polar coarea and the replica norm density. -> projection and pair tails
- **step-limit-growth** [claim](#stmt-edge-limit-growth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-limit-growth): Transfer finite-n counting bounds to the limiting edge process and invert. -> two-sided power growth of edge rates
- **step-overlap-cells** [claim](#stmt-edge-gram-cell) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-gram-cell): Stirling bounds for binomial mass and spherical density. -> cell mass comparison
- **step-haar-moment** [claim](#stmt-edge-replica-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-replica-comparison): Weighted cell comparison and pair tails combined with the global input. -> Haar second moment bound
- **step-cube-caps** [claim](#stmt-edge-cube-caps) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-cube-caps): Net argument with Chebyshev and interpolation of the log partition function. -> uniform cube cap estimates
- **step-annuli** [claim](#stmt-edge-path-annuli) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-path-annuli): Quadratic-form concentration, mesh interpolation and a change of Gaussian reference. -> annulus location of the observation path
- **step-score-covariance** [claim](#stmt-edge-score-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-score-covariance): Likelihood martingale and integrated Ito identity. -> score and Frobenius bounds
- **step-annular-extension** [claim](#stmt-edge-annular-extension) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-annular-extension): Infimum of supporting quadratics and frozen-saddle reference transition. -> semiconcave extension
- **step-positive-curvature** [claim](#stmt-edge-positive-curvature) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-positive-curvature): Parent-child covariance iteration with Haar compression and a barrier. -> positive covariance error bound
- **step-cap-estimates** [claim](#stmt-prop-edge-estimates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-edge-positive-curvature-2): Variance differential inequality with amplification factor using curvature bounds. -> cap estimates with tight threshold
- **step-small-profile** [claim](#stmt-warm-small-profile) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-small-profile): Contradiction using observation entropy, bridge loss and a log-Sobolev criterion. -> small-entropy dissipation profile
- **step-product-endpoint** [claim](#stmt-warm-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-product): Tensorized two-point log-Sobolev bound and concavity of the edge weight. -> endpoint entropy bounds
- **step-posterior-mean** [claim](#stmt-warm-posterior-mean) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-posterior-mean): One-site integration by parts and induction over residual recipes. -> square-root energy posterior-mean bound
- **step-large-retention** [claim](#stmt-warm-large-retention) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-large-retention): Observation path to a product posterior with stopped entropy accounting. -> extensive endpoint entropy
- **step-dissipation-profiles** [claim](#stmt-warm-profiles) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-large-retention-2): Three entropy ranges treated by the two-observation argument, the proportional branch, and the product endpoint. -> restricted dissipation profiles
- **step-log-level** [claim](#stmt-warm-log-layer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-log-layer): Truncation of a density at a logarithmic level and data processing. -> bounded level test
- **step-entropy-dissipation** [claim](#stmt-warm-entropy-profile) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-entropy-profile): Geometric summation over levels and the level test. -> entropy dissipation power law
- **step-support-profile** [claim](#stmt-warm-support-profile) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-support-profile): Equal-height layers and dyadic decomposition using the classical profile. -> support energy profile
- **step-warming-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-warming) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-support-profile-2): Differential inequalities for entropy, square mass and a convex logarithmic moment. -> entropy, kernel and log-moment bounds
- **step-kernel-tail** [claim](#stmt-warm-kernel-log-tail) / [proof](#proof-stmt-warm-kernel-log-tail): Markov inequality applied to the logarithmic moment bound. -> polynomial tail of the kernel logarithm
- **step-gaussian-subsequence** [claim](#stmt-prop-gaussian-subsequence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-gaussian-subsequence): Variational resolvent convergence, density extraction and tail control of two equilibrium copies. -> subsequential Gaussian limits
- **step-seed-escape** [claim](#stmt-prop-uniform-seed-escape) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-uniform-seed-escape): Stopped Haar rotation at fixed spectrum plus a lower tail of the weighted size. -> escape estimate
- **step-angular-realization** [claim](#stmt-entr-angular-realization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-entr-angular-realization): Quasi-regular Dirichlet form diffusion and Fukushima decomposition. -> angular stochastic equation
- **step-resolvent-kernels** [claim](#stmt-entr-kernels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-entr-kernels): Stieltjes representation of the resolvent transform. -> kernel bounds and inversion
- **step-stochastic-kernels** [claim](#stmt-entr-stochastic-kernels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-entr-stochastic-kernels): Burkholder-Davis-Gundy bounds and chaining. -> stochastic convolution bounds
- **step-volterra** [claim](#stmt-entr-volterra) / [proof](#proof-stmt-entr-volterra): Finite-N identity, kernel inversion and passage to the limit by localization. -> Volterra equation
- **step-escaping-seeds** [claim](#stmt-entr-escaping-seeds) / [proof](#proof-stmt-entr-escaping-seeds): Convex combination of kernels and dominated convergence. -> seed response limit
- **step-entrance-selection** [claim](#stmt-thm-entrance-selection) / [proof](#pm-h-36): Coupling of two entrance diffusions through stopped contraction and total variation. -> uniqueness, zero boundary and measurable family
- **step-static-support** [claim](#stmt-hist-static-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-static-support): Product of smooth factors of replica probabilities and overlap tails by cell comparison. -> static cutoff
- **step-cutoff-hazards** [claim](#stmt-hist-cutoff-hazards) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-cutoff-hazards): Logistic cap of an affine function with explicit derivatives. -> smooth caps
- **step-kernel-caps** [claim](#stmt-hist-kernel-caps) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-kernel-caps): Induction on the tree with the semigroup property. -> capped kernels
- **step-gaussian-survival** [claim](#stmt-hist-gaussian-survival) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-gaussian-survival): Log-moment warming bound with Markov inequality and a union over nodes. -> negligible check loss
- **step-conditional-interior** [claim](#stmt-hist-conditional-interior) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-conditional-interior): Laminar tree structure and the Markov property. -> bridge law and prefix density
- **step-history-overlaps** [claim](#stmt-hist-history-overlaps) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-history-overlaps): Kernel cap density bound with static overlap tails and a mesh argument. -> path overlap bounds
- **step-crude-coefficients** [claim](#stmt-hist-crude-ratios) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hist-crude-ratios): Polynomial lower bound on leaf transitions propagated up the tree. -> coarse coefficient bounds
- **step-hellinger** [claim](#stmt-score-hellinger) / [proof](#proof-stmt-score-hellinger): Likelihood supermartingale and Fatou localization. -> intensity cost bounds
- **step-raw-size** [claim](#stmt-score-raw-size) / [proof](#proof-stmt-score-raw-size): Martingale square-function bounds and detailed balance. -> raw coefficient bounds
- **step-one-insertion** [claim](#stmt-score-one-insertion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-score-one-insertion): Overlap kernel estimates on blocks after compensation. -> single-insertion bounds
- **step-raw-projection** [claim](#stmt-score-raw-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-score-raw-projection): Dyadic decomposition of ring insertions with compensation. -> raw representation
- **step-clock-scores** [claim](#stmt-prop-clock-scores) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-clock-scores): Joint induction on the order using the midpoint identity. -> conditional score bounds
- **step-history-derivatives** [claim](#stmt-repl-history-derivatives) / [proof](#proof-stmt-repl-history-derivatives): Expansion at cutoff marks with copies of interiors and Holder allocation. -> averaged history derivative bounds
- **step-observable-derivatives** [claim](#stmt-repl-observable-derivatives) / [proof](#proof-stmt-repl-observable-derivatives): Chain rule on the cutoff and test, summing history derivative bounds. -> observable derivative bounds
- **step-entrywise-replacement** [claim](#stmt-repl-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-repl-comparison): Mixture interpolation with Taylor expansion to the fourth order. -> Gaussian-Rademacher comparison
- **step-rademacher-transfer** [claim](#stmt-prop-universality) / [proof](#pm-h-59): Removal of cutoffs, grid interpolation with smoothed maxima and tightness. -> Rademacher functional limit
- **step-main-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-repl-comparison-2): Assembly of warming, subsequential limits, entrance selection and universality. -> critical quench universality

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **inv-main-joint-limit**: For almost every edge realization there is a measurable family of probability densities relative to the conditioned edge measure such that the stationary and quench autocorrelations converge jointly in law, with the same limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings, and the quench limit relaxes to the stationary limit as the waiting time grows.
- **inv-stationary-inputs**: The edge law, its conditioned cylinder densities, the closability of the gradient form and the relaxed-energy liminf and recovery properties are the stationary inputs on which the quench analysis rests.
- **inv-warming-bounds**: On Gaussian disorder events of high limiting probability, entropy, heat-kernel and logarithmic-moment bounds hold at every positive critical time uniformly over the initial law.
- **inv-entrance-uniqueness**: At most one family of positive-time densities with the semigroup property, local boundedness and sequential escape of the seed weights exists, and any such family converges to the point mass at zero in the product topology as the time tends to zero.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-nonzero-field**: Applying the critical scaling and the limiting edge semigroup to a spin system with an external magnetic field. -> The edge limit and the identified relaxation operator are derived for the zero-field Gibbs measure; a field changes the measure and the claimed limit is not established.
- **anti-other-coupling-laws**: Transferring the limit to arbitrary coupling laws, such as sparse or heavy-tailed interactions. -> Only the Gaussian and the symmetric sign law are covered; the entry-replacement comparison uses their moment matching.
- **anti-other-time-scale**: Reading the limit at waiting times or lags unrelated to the critical unit, or at other temperatures. -> The relaxation time grows with the system size at the critical temperature and the limit is stated in that unit; other regimes need different scalings.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The paper proves asymptotic convergence in law of the stationary and quench autocorrelations to a random limit and identifies an entrance family of densities on an infinite-dimensional conditioned measure. The entrance family is obtained by abstract uniqueness and measurable selection arguments, so there is no finite procedure that computes the limit, and no input-output contract with a terminating computation exists to be checked by an independent oracle.

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-coupling-law** (hypothesis): The theorem is stated only for couplings that are standard Gaussian or uniform on the two signs. No other coupling law is covered. Blocked use: ['Transferring the limit to sparse, heavy-tailed or otherwise non-Gaussian, non-sign interaction laws', 'Using the result for models whose couplings are not independent symmetric entries with zero diagonal']
- **limit-critical-time-scale** (hypothesis): The limit is formulated at the critical temperature, where the relaxation time grows with the number of spins. Waiting times and lags are measured in the critical unit, so the statement says nothing about other temperatures or other time units. Blocked use: ['Reading the limiting curves at temperatures other than the critical one', 'Applying the limit to times not measured in the critical unit']
- **limit-uniform-quench-start** (hypothesis): The quench limit is derived for the uniform initial law on the cube, independent of the couplings. The selected entrance family is tied to that initial state, so other initial laws are not covered by the identification. Blocked use: ['Using the quench limit for non-uniform or coupling-dependent initial states', 'Assuming the same entrance family for arbitrary starts']
- **limit-independent-clocks** (hypothesis): The dynamics are single-site heat-bath updates driven by independent site clocks of the same rate. Other update rules or synchronous schemes are not covered. Blocked use: ['Applying the limit to Metropolis or parallel update schemes without a separate argument', 'Rescaling time with non-uniform site rates']
- **limit-gaussian-warming** (formal_scope): The warming, entropy and kernel bounds, and the cap estimates behind them, are proved for Gaussian couplings on disorder events of high but not full limiting probability. They are not stated for the sign law, which is reached only by the later entry-replacement comparison. Blocked use: ['Quoting the warming bounds as proved directly for sign couplings', 'Treating the disorder events as holding for every realization']
- **limit-gaussian-stationary-inputs** (formal_scope): The stationary inputs for the finite models are used in the Gaussian setting with the completed diagonal until the disorder comparison, so the intermediate steps are not valid for sign couplings. Blocked use: ['Applying the spectral coordinate identities of the completed matrix directly to sign couplings']
- **limit-tight-threshold** (approximation): Cap and warming estimates hold with tight constants and a tight lower threshold on the active dimension, valid on events of limiting probability close to one. The thresholds are not explicit, so the estimates carry no usable numerical values. Blocked use: ['Extracting explicit finite-size error bars from the estimates', 'Using the bounds below the stated threshold on the active dimension']
- **limit-nonconstructive-entrance** (nonconstructive): The entrance family exists only for almost every edge realization and is obtained by uniqueness and measurable selection arguments. It is not given by a formula or algorithm. Blocked use: ['Computing the densities by a finite procedure from the theorem', 'Claiming existence for every edge realization']
- **limit-edge-shift-positivity** (edge_case): The growth bounds for the limiting edge coordinates require a shift b with b+g_1>0 and hold only for almost every edge realization, with constants depending on g and b. <a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove joint functional convergence of the stationary and quench autocorrelations of zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick heat-bath dynamics at inverse temperature <i>β</i> = 1, with the same random limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. Each site has a rate-one clock, mean spin autocorrelations are multiplied by <i>n</i><sup>1/3</sup>, and waiting times and lags are measured in units <i>n</i><sup>2/3</sup>. The quench starts from independent fair spins, and convergence is uniform on compact sets of positive waiting times and lags. The quench limit is selected by these initial states and relaxes to the stationary limiting autocorrelation as the waiting time tends to infinity.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

A quench starts a spin system from a simple nonequilibrium law and then lets it evolve at a prescribed temperature. At the critical temperature of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model, the relevant relaxation time grows with the number of spins. We determine the two-time autocorrelation after a quench from independent symmetric spins. The limit retains the random spectral edge of the interaction matrix and is governed by the same diffusion as the stationary critical autocorrelation.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The model and the result

<a id="eq:finite-A"></a>
<a id="eq:finite-B"></a>
Let $D$ be either the standard Gaussian law or the uniform law on $\{-1,1\}$. For $n\ge2$, let $J_{ij}$, $i<j$, be independent with law $D$, and put $J_{ji}=J_{ij}$, $J_{ii}=0$. The critical zero-field Gibbs measure is <a id="eq:gibbs"></a>$$\label{eq:gibbs}
 \pi_{n,J}(\sigma)
 =Z_{n,J}^{-1}
   \exp\left\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j\right\},
 \qquad \sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n .$$ Every site has an independent rate-one clock. At a ring at site $i$, its spin is replaced by $a\in\{-1,1\}$ with conditional probability $$\frac{\exp(a h_i(\sigma))}{2\cosh h_i(\sigma)},
 \qquad
 h_i(\sigma)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{j\ne i}J_{ij}\sigma_j .$$ Write $P_t^J$ for this heat-bath semigroup. Thus one unit of time contains $n$ updates on average. Let $\nu_n$ be the uniform law on the cube, independent of $J$, and set $T_n=n^{2/3}$. The stationary and quench autocorrelations in critical units are, respectively, $$\begin{aligned}
 A_{n,J}(t)
   &=n^{-2/3}\sum_{i=1}^n
      \langle \sigma_i,P_{tT_n}^J\sigma_i\rangle_{\pi_{n,J}},
       \qquad t>0,                                      \label{eq:finite-A}\\
 B_{n,J}(s,t)
   &=n^{-2/3}\sum_{i=1}^n
      \mathbb E_{\nu_n}^J[\sigma_i(sT_n)\sigma_i((s+t)T_n)],
       \qquad s,t>0.                                    \label{eq:finite-B}
\end{aligned}$$ Thermal and clock randomness are averaged in these functions; the interaction $J$ remains random. The variable $s$ is the waiting time after the quench and $t$ is the subsequent lag.

<a id="eq:edge-semigroup"></a>
We recall the edge data of the stationary theorem (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 2.3, Proposition 5.1, and Theorem 6.8) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. Let $g=(g_a)_{a\ge1}$ be the increasing upper GOE edge process, the joint limit in law of the leading coordinates: for each fixed $m$, $$\bigl(n^{2/3}(2-\lambda_a)\bigr)_{a=1}^m
       \ \Longrightarrow\ (g_a)_{a=1}^m ,$$ where $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots$ are the eigenvalues of a GOE matrix with off-diagonal variance $1/n$ (Ramírez, Rider, and Virág 2011, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[RamirezRiderVirag2011](#ref-RamirezRiderVirag2011)]. For any $b+g_1>0$, put $\ell_a=(g_a+b)^{-1}$ and <a id="eq:edge-D-intro"></a>$$\label{eq:edge-D-intro}
 D_g(b)=\lim_{L\to\infty}
 \left\{\sqrt L-\sum_{a\ge1}
 \left(\frac1{g_a+b}-\frac1{g_a+L}\right)\right\}.$$ The limit is in probability over $g$, with the almost-sure version chosen along a deterministic sequence as in the cited stationary theorem. If $Z_a$ are independent $N(0,\ell_a)$, their centered square sum converges. The continuous densities of this sum and its tails define $$\Pi_g=\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}\left((Z_a)_{a\ge1}\,\middle|\,
              \sum_{a\ge1}(Z_a^2-\ell_a)=D_g(b)\right).$$ This measure is independent of the admissible $b$. The cylinder gradient form $$\mathcal E_g(F)=\int\sum_{a\ge1}|\partial_aF|^2\,\,\mathrm d\Pi_g$$ is closable. Let $H_g$ be the nonnegative operator of its closure, and let $c_*>0$ be the deterministic microscopic coefficient in (OpenAI 2026d, Theorem 6.8) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. We write $$\label{eq:edge-semigroup}
 S_t^g=e^{-t c_*H_g},
 \qquad
 A_g(t)=\sum_{a\ge1}\langle x_a,S_t^g x_a\rangle_{\Pi_g},\quad t>0.$$ The stationary theorem gives a Borel version of $A_g$ in $C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))$. Section <a href="#sec:background" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:background">2</a> records the finite normalization and the stationary edge, static-coordinate, and relaxed-energy inputs.

For an open set $V\subset\mathbb R^d$, $C_{\mathrm{loc}}(V)$ denotes the space of continuous functions with uniform convergence on every compact subset. Fix the countable family $\mathcal{V}$ of bounded smooth cylinder tests constructed in Section <a href="#sec:gaussian-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gaussian-limits">5</a>. It is dense in $L^2(\Pi_g)$ for each edge realization under consideration. We call a family $h_s^g\in L^2(\Pi_g)$ measurable when $(g,s)\mapsto\Pi_g[h_s^g\phi]$ is measurable for each test $\phi\in\mathcal{V}$. These pairings determine each density class.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Critical quench universality). *There is a measurable family $(h_s^g)_{s>0}$, with $h_s^g\in L^2(\Pi_g)$, such that for almost every $g$ the following properties hold.*

1.  *For every $s>0$, $h_s^g\ge0$ and $\Pi_g[h_s^g]=1$. For $s,t>0$, $$h_{s+t}^g=S_t^g h_s^g.$$ Moreover, $$h_s^g\Pi_g\ \Longrightarrow\ \delta_0
           \quad\text{in the product topology on }\mathbb R^\mathbb N
           \quad(s\downarrow0),
           \qquad
           \|h_s^g-1\|_{L^1(\Pi_g)}\longrightarrow0
           \quad(s\to\infty).$$*

2.  *The series <a id="eq:limit-B"></a>$$\label{eq:limit-B}
           B_g(s,t)=\sum_{a\ge1}
              \int h_s^g(x)\,x_a\,(S_t^g x_a)(x)\,\,\mathrm d\Pi_g(x)$$ converges locally uniformly on $(0,\infty)^2$ and defines a continuous function.*

3.  *For both choices of $D$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}_D(A_{n,J},B_{n,J})
           \ \Longrightarrow\
           \mathop{\mathrm{Law}}_g(A_g,B_g)$$ in $C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))
            \times C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty)^2)$. The two coupling laws have the same $g$, the same family $h^g$, and the same coefficient $c_*$.*

4.  *For every $0<a<b<\infty$, $$\sup_{a\le t\le b}|B_g(s,t)-A_g(t)|
              \longrightarrow0
           \quad\text{in probability over }g
           \quad(s\to\infty).$$*

*The positive-time density limits of the Gaussian dynamics with initial law $\nu_n$ select this family, as made precise in Theorem <a href="#thm:entrance-selection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:entrance-selection">27</a>. The normalization is exactly <a href="#eq:finite-A" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-A">[eq:finite-A]</a>–<a href="#eq:finite-B" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-B">[eq:finite-B]</a>.*

</div>

The boundary $\delta_0$ is interpreted in the product topology. At small times each fixed edge coordinate can vanish while the renormalized constraint is carried by coordinates whose indices tend to infinity. The proof identifies which such entrance is selected by the uniform starts through a stronger, quantitative condition on these coordinates.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### History and significance

Sherrington and Kirkpatrick introduced the infinite-range spin-glass model in 1975 (Sherrington and Kirkpatrick 1975) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[SK1975](#ref-SK1975)]. The subsequent dynamical theory studied memory through two-time correlation and response functions. In particular, Sompolinsky and Zippelius developed a dynamical mean-field treatment for soft spins (Sompolinsky and Zippelius 1982) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[SompolinskyZippelius1982](#ref-SompolinskyZippelius1982)], and Cugliandolo and Kurchan analyzed nonequilibrium relaxation after a quench in a soft-spin Langevin formulation (Cugliandolo and Kurchan 1994) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[CugliandoloKurchan1994](#ref-CugliandoloKurchan1994)]. Their asymptotic regime takes the system-size limit before the long-time limit and differs from the finite-size critical window considered here. For critical Ising heat-bath dynamics, Billoire and Campbell (Billoire and Campbell 2011, Equation (7)) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[BilloireCampbell2011](#ref-BilloireCampbell2011)] numerically tested the stationary finite-size form $$q_c(n,t)\sim n^{-1/3}F(t/n^{2/3}),$$ with time measured in updates per spin. Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> studies the two positive times following a uniform quench and identifies the law of the sample-dependent limiting function.

The spectral mechanism is especially transparent in spherical spin glasses. Kosterlitz, Thouless, and Jones (Kosterlitz, Thouless, and Jones 1976) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[KosterlitzThoulessJones1976](#ref-KosterlitzThoulessJones1976)] analyzed the infinite-range Gaussian spherical spin glass using properties of large random matrices. Cugliandolo and Dean (Cugliandolo and Dean 1995) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[CugliandoloDean1995](#ref-CugliandoloDean1995)] studied relaxation and aging for the spherical model, while Ben Arous, Dembo, and Guionnet (Ben Arous, Dembo, and Guionnet 2001) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BenArousDemboGuionnet2001](#ref-BenArousDemboGuionnet2001)] proved limiting dynamical and aging results with a soft spherical constraint. Fyodorov, Perret, and Schehr (Fyodorov, Perret, and Schehr 2015) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[FyodorovPerretSchehr2015](#ref-FyodorovPerretSchehr2015)] later connected finite-size randomness on the $n^{2/3}$ scale to the edge in zero-temperature spherical dynamics. These works concern different spin spaces or temperature regimes; they explain why the critical edge should remain visible in a nonequilibrium limit.

The stationary critical Ising theorem (OpenAI 2026d) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] identifies the conditioned edge measure, its closed dynamical form, and the microscopic coefficient $c_*$. Its equilibrium comparison uses the conditional eigenframe averaging of Comets (Comets 1996, Equations (2.1)–(2.2)) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Comets1996](#ref-Comets1996)], which equates the Haar-averaged cube and spherical partition integrals when both use normalized reference measures and the same quadratic Hamiltonian, and the critical conditioned-Gaussian description of Du and Huang (Du and Huang 2026a, 2026b) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[DuHuang2026FreeEnergy](#ref-DuHuang2026FreeEnergy), [DuHuang2026Overlap](#ref-DuHuang2026Overlap)]. Using the cap and spectral estimates of (OpenAI 2026d, 2026b, 2026c) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA), [CM](#ref-CM), [CS](#ref-CS)], Sections <a href="#sec:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:edge-estimates">3</a> and <a href="#sec:warming" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:warming">4</a> extend cap control down to a tight lower threshold for $np^3$ and derive warming uniformly over the initial law at each positive critical time. The order-$n$ entropy argument uses Lemma <a href="#warm:posterior-mean" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="warm:posterior-mean">19</a>, which strengthens the square-density posterior-mean estimate of (OpenAI 2026a, Proposition 7.3) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[SG](#ref-SG)] to square-root dependence on the relative heat-bath energy. The stationary relaxed-energy theorem is applied within its polynomially bounded test class through bounded resolvent optimizers in Section <a href="#sec:gaussian-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gaussian-limits">5</a>.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### The argument

In the Gaussian model, adding an independent GOE diagonal changes the spin Hamiltonian only by a constant. Let $u_a$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of the completed matrix and put $x_a=n^{-1/3}\langle u_a,\sigma\rangle$. If $w_s$ is the Gibbs-relative density at time $sT_n$, orthogonality rewrites the quench correlation as $$B_{n,J}(s,t)=\sum_{a=1}^n
       \pi_{n,J}[w_s\,x_a\,P_{tT_n}^Jx_a].$$ This formula separates the law reached after the quench from subsequent relaxation. The source identifies the relaxation operator for sufficiently controlled tests. Three further arguments are needed.

We first regularize the law reached after the quench. At scale $p$, a nested Gaussian observation gives noisy information about the spin projections onto modes with $2-\lambda_a\le p^2$; conditioning caps those eigenvalues at $2-p^2$. On the retained spectral events, their number is comparable to $k_p=np^3$. Section <a href="#sec:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:edge-estimates">3</a> bounds the variance left unresolved for $0\le f\le1$ by $Cp^{-2}$ times the heat-bath energy plus $Ce^{-ck_p^a}$, down to a fixed threshold for $k_p$ at each prescribed disorder confidence. In the small-entropy part of Section <a href="#sec:warming" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:warming">4</a>, a contradiction argument assumes that a bounded level test $f$ has less energy than the claimed profile bound. At a later scale $R$, this makes the normalized tilt by $f^2$ close to the normalized observation tilt by $F_R^2$, where $F_R=\mathbb E[f\mid h_R]$. Following its entropy through earlier observations, together with the source path to a product posterior at higher entropy levels, yields entropy and kernel bounds at every fixed positive critical time, uniformly over the initial law.

For bounded cylinder sources, the finite Markov resolvent contraction bounds the optimizers used in the stationary relaxed-energy theorem. Section <a href="#sec:gaussian-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gaussian-limits">5</a> derives strong semigroup convergence from that theorem and combines it with the warming bounds on densities and transition kernels. This produces positive-time families on represented Gaussian subsequences, evolving by $S_t^g$, which may initially retain randomness beyond $g$. To select one, choose a measurable admissible $b$ with $D_g(b)>0$, put $r_i=g_i+b$, and define $$M_g(x)=\sum_i\frac{x_i^2}{2r_i}.$$ We prove that $0<M_g(x)<\infty$ for $\Pi_g$-almost every $x$ and therefore may define, on that full-measure set, the probability weights $$p_i(x)=\frac{x_i^2}{2r_iM_g(x)}.$$ For each represented Gaussian limit, the averaged uniform-start estimate yields a deterministic sequence $s_k\downarrow0$ along which these weights leave every fixed finite set in probability under $h_{s_k}\Pi_g$, almost surely in the represented data. Section <a href="#sec:entrance-selection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:entrance-selection">6</a> considers semigroup families whose densities are locally uniformly bounded in $L^\infty(\Pi_g)$ and satisfy such sequential escape. Angular ratios and a common rescaling give linear mode equations driven by independent Brownian motions with a common diffusion factor. The square constraint gives a scalar Volterra equation whose high-mode responses approach a common kernel. A stopped coupling proves fixed-$g$ uniqueness and the full $s\downarrow0$ product-topology boundary. The proof then constructs the common family measurably from $g$.

Finally, we compare smooth functions of the stationary and quench traces under entry replacement (Chatterjee 2006) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[Chatterjee2006](#ref-Chatterjee2006)]. An order-$k$ derivative with respect to the normalized interaction $J_{ij}/\sqrt n$ is accompanied by $n^{-k/2}$, while summing over entries contributes order $n^2$. The two coupling laws match through order three, so the averaged fourth derivative must gain a vanishing factor. Sections <a href="#sec:history-cutoffs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:history-cutoffs">7</a>–<a href="#sec:replacement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:replacement">9</a> first impose static overlap-tail estimates for every interaction matrix in a cutoff’s support. Under the associated normalized weighted path laws, these estimates yield history-overlap bounds with failure probability $O(n^{-A})$ for any prescribed $A>0$, after the cutoff parameters are chosen. Forward and reverse conditional estimates for endpoint-normalized likelihoods on a binary tree of transition intervals then control the derivatives over the full critical time span. The estimates also include derivatives of the cutoff weights. They transfer the joint trace laws and the probability of retaining the cutoffs to Rademacher disorder; smooth grid tests then transfer tightness in the locally uniform topology. Section <a href="#sec:completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:completion">10</a> assembles the result.

<a id="sec:background"></a>
### The stationary edge input

We fix the finite normalization and record the stationary edge, static-comparison, and relaxed-energy inputs used below. Source cap estimates are stated at their points of use in Section <a href="#sec:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:edge-estimates">3</a>; the following sections develop the extensions, entrance construction, and disorder comparison.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### The finite form and spectral coordinates

<a id="eq:finite-form"></a>
Write $\mu=\pi_{n,J}$. For a function $f$ on the cube let $$D_i f(\sigma)=\frac{f(\sigma^{i,+})-f(\sigma^{i,-})}{2},
 \qquad
 t_i(\sigma)=\tanh h_i(\sigma),\qquad
 v_i(\sigma)=1-t_i(\sigma)^2,$$ where $\sigma^{i,\pm}$ is obtained by setting spin $i$ to $\pm1$. The nonnegative heat-bath operator and its symmetric form are $$\label{eq:finite-form}
 H_n=\sum_{i=1}^n(\sigma_i-t_i)D_i,\qquad
 \mathcal E(f,k)=\mu\left[\sum_{i=1}^n v_iD_ifD_ik\right],
 \qquad P_t^J=e^{-tH_n}.$$ Indeed the summand of $H_n$ is $f-\mu[f\mid\sigma_{-i}]$. Conditional two-point covariance gives the displayed form. Thus <a href="#eq:finite-form" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-form">[eq:finite-form]</a> uses the rate-one clock at each site specified in the theorem. We write $\mathcal E(f)=\mathcal E(f,f)$ and, for $z\ge0$, $\mathcal I(z)=\mathcal E(z,\log z)$, with its extended nonnegative value at zeros.

Until the disorder comparison, $J$ is Gaussian. Put $W_{ij}=J_{ij}/\sqrt n$ off the diagonal and add independent $W_{ii}\sim N(0,2/n)$. The diagonal contributes a constant to $\sigma^{\mathsf T}W\sigma/2$, so neither $\mu$ nor $H_n$ changes. After independent sign choices for the eigenvectors, $$W=U\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n,$$ has $U$ Haar orthogonal conditionally on the eigenvalues. Denote its columns by $u_a$, and put <a id="eq:finite-edge"></a>$$\label{eq:finite-edge}
 d_a=2-\lambda_a,\qquad g_{a,n}=T_n d_a,\qquad
 x_a(\sigma)=n^{-1/3}\langle u_a,\sigma\rangle .$$ We use the same $x_a$ for the coordinate functions on $\mathbb R^\mathbb N$. For two spins, orthogonality gives the exact identity <a id="eq:replica-identity"></a>$$\label{eq:replica-identity}
 n^{-2/3}\sigma\cdot\sigma'
       =\sum_{a=1}^n x_a(\sigma)x_a(\sigma').$$ In particular, if $w_s=d(\nu_nP_{sT_n}^J)/d\mu$, then <a id="eq:finite-spectral-traces"></a>$$\label{eq:finite-spectral-traces}
 A_{n,J}(t)=\sum_{a=1}^n\mu[x_aP_{tT_n}^Jx_a],
 \qquad
 B_{n,J}(s,t)=\sum_{a=1}^n\mu[w_sx_aP_{tT_n}^Jx_a].$$

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Conditioned measure and relaxed energy

The following statements are the parts of the stationary manuscript that we use directly. They also specify the meaning of the conditional measure in the introduction. A smooth compact cylinder is a smooth function of finitely many coordinates, compactly supported in those coordinates.

<a id="stmt-prop-stationary-inputs"></a>
<div id="prop:stationary-inputs" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2** (Stationary inputs). *The following hold for the edge law and the Gaussian finite models.*

1.  *Let $b+g_1>0$, $\ell_a=(g_a+b)^{-1}$. Almost surely $\sum_a\ell_a=\infty$ and $\sum_a\ell_a^2<\infty$. If $Z_a$ are independent $N(0,\ell_a)$, the densities $q$ of $\sum_a(Z_a^2-\ell_a)$ and $q_m$ of $\sum_{a>m}(Z_a^2-\ell_a)$ are continuous, bounded, and strictly positive. The first $m$ coordinates of $\Pi_g$ have density <a id="eq:edge-cylinder-density"></a>$$\label{eq:edge-cylinder-density}
           \frac{q_m\!\left(D_g(b)-\sum_{a\le m}(x_a^2-\ell_a)\right)}
                {q(D_g(b))}
           \prod_{a\le m}
              \frac{e^{-x_a^2/(2\ell_a)}}{\sqrt{2\pi\ell_a}}.$$ These consistent densities are measurable in $g$ and independent of $b$. For each fixed $0\le j<\infty$, $\Pi_g[|x_a|^j]\le C_{j,g,b}\ell_a^{j/2}$, with a finite constant uniform in $a$. For sufficiently large fixed $m$, the tail beyond $m$ has a density bounded by a finite constant relative to $\bigotimes_{a>m}N(0,\ell_a)$. Conditional on that tail, the first $m$ coordinates have the Gaussian angular law on the sphere of squared radius $$D_g(b)+\sum_{a\le m}\ell_a-\sum_{a>m}(x_a^2-\ell_a).$$ In particular the renormalized constraint holds $\Pi_g$-almost surely. These are the statements of (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 2.3) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)].*

2.  *With $b_n=1+(-g_{1,n})_+$ and $b=1+(-g_1)_+$, the spherical and cube edge marginals converge jointly with the edge points to $\Pi_g$ on the represented subsequences described below. Cube integrals converge for every continuous cylinder of polynomial growth. Spherical coordinates obey the uniform bounds $$\mu^{\mathrm{sp}}[|x_a|^j]\le C_j(g_{a,n}+b_n)^{-j/2},
           \qquad
           \lim_{m\to\infty}\sup_n\sum_{a>m}(g_{a,n}+b_n)^{-2}=0$$ after discarding finitely many $n$ on such a representation. Here $\mu^{\mathrm{sp}}$ is surface measure on $\{|\sigma|^2=n\}$, tilted by $\exp(\sigma^{\mathsf T}W\sigma/2)$. The sources are (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 3.3) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)].*

3.  *The Euclidean gradient on smooth compact cylinders is closable from $L^2(\Pi_g)$ to $L^2(\Pi_g;\ell^2)$. The associated closed form has kernel equal to the constants. Every coordinate belongs to its domain and satisfies $\nabla x_a=e_a$, hence $\mathcal E_g(x_a)=1$. This is (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 5.1) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. The usual contraction rule for gradients passes to the closure, so the form is Dirichlet and $S_t^g$ is a conservative symmetric Markov semigroup.*

<a id="eq:relaxed-liminf"></a>
4.  *On a quenched represented subsequence, say that $f_n$ converges weakly to $F\in L^2(\Pi_g)$ if its $L^2(\mu)$ norms are bounded and $\mu[f_n\phi(x)]\to\Pi_g[F\phi]$ for every smooth compact cylinder $\phi$; call the convergence strong when in addition $\mu[f_n^2]\to\Pi_g[F^2]$. Suppose, for fixed $C,D<\infty$, that $\|f_n\|_\infty\le Cn^D$, that $T_n\mathcal E(f_n)$ is bounded, and that $f_n$ converges weakly to $F$. Then $F$ belongs to the closed form domain and $$\label{eq:relaxed-liminf}
           \liminf_n T_n\mathcal E(f_n)\ge c_*\mathcal E_g(F).$$ Conversely, for every smooth compact cylinder $F$, there are functions $f_{n,j}$, polynomially bounded for each fixed $j$, such that $f_{n,j}$ converges strongly to $F$ as $n\to\infty$ for each $j$, and <a id="eq:relaxed-recovery"></a>$$\label{eq:relaxed-recovery}
           \lim_{j\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}T_n\mathcal E(f_{n,j})
              =c_*\mathcal E_g(F).$$ The source asserts a common represented event for countably many chosen sources and tests. Recovery is used at each fixed $j$, followed by the displayed $j$-limit (OpenAI 2026d, Theorem 6.8) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)].*

</div>

In Item 1, the tail density is $$\frac{q_m^{\mathrm{head}}\!\left(
     D_g(b)-\sum_{a>m}(x_a^2-\ell_a)\right)}{q(D_g(b))},$$ where $q_m^{\mathrm{head}}$ is the density of the centered head square sum. A sufficiently large head makes this density bounded. This concrete description will be used for estimates on infinitely many coordinates. For a candidate pair $(F,G)\in L^2(\Pi_g)\times L^2(\Pi_g;\ell^2)$, the angular weak identity underlying Item 3 is <a id="eq:angular-weak"></a>$$\label{eq:angular-weak}
 \int \psi\,(Ax)\cdot G\,\,\mathrm d\Pi_g
 =-\int F\left\{(Ax)\cdot\nabla\psi
       -\psi\sum_a(g_a+b)x_a(Ax)_a\right\}\,\mathrm d\Pi_g ,$$ for every skew-symmetric matrix $A$ with finitely many nonzero entries and every smooth compact cylinder $\psi$ whose coordinate set contains every index appearing in $A$. These identities hold exactly when $F$ belongs to the closed form domain and $G=\nabla F$ (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 5.1) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. The term with $b$ cancels by skew-symmetry.

The source also proves that $g\mapsto A_g$, defined in <a href="#eq:edge-semigroup" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:edge-semigroup">[eq:edge-semigroup]</a>, is a Borel $C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))$-valued map and identifies $A_g$ as the stationary limit for both entry laws (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 9.2) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. We will obtain the joint limit with $B_{n,J}$ from the same finite coordinates. In particular, <a href="#eq:relaxed-liminf" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:relaxed-liminf">[eq:relaxed-liminf]</a> is used with its polynomial bound; the strong resolvent convergence needed here is derived in Section <a href="#sec:gaussian-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gaussian-limits">5</a>.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### High-probability estimates and subsequences

We make one convention for random constants. An estimate holds with *tight constants* if, for every $\chi>0$, there are deterministic constants in that estimate and events $\mathcal G_{n,\chi}$ such that $$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(\mathcal G_{n,\chi})\ge1-\chi$$ and the estimate holds on $\mathcal G_{n,\chi}$ simultaneously for every scale and test function in its stated class. The constants may depend on $\chi$ and on fixed parameters specified before the estimate, but not on $n$, the scale, or the test. A tight lower threshold for the dimension parameter $k_p=np^3$ has the same meaning with a deterministic threshold $K_\chi$ on each event. When an estimate is required above a vanishing time threshold, this means that for each $\chi$ a deterministic threshold $\varepsilon_{n,\chi}\downarrow0$ can be chosen on those events.

We use the represented-subsequence convention of (OpenAI 2026d, Remark 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. The edge points, the countably many cylinder integrals and error quantities in use, and bounds that are tight in the preceding sense are included in a joint law before applying the subsequence and Skorokhod representation theorems. A further diagonal subsequence handles an iterated limit such as $\lim_{m\to\infty}\limsup_n$. On the resulting probability space, the relevant bounds are finite and the chosen coordinates converge almost surely. Conditional laws of the remaining finite data recover the original finite models. This construction is used only to show that every subsequence has a further subsequence with the identified limit, which implies the asserted convergence in law.

For a disorder-dependent test, we use the separate class-uniform quenched convention of (OpenAI 2026d, Remark 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]: each invoked inequality holds on one event for every test in its stated norm, energy, and polynomial-growth class. The source obtains this uniformity by bounding the error by the stated norms times a common nonnegative random error, which permits measurable choices of the test. The common represented event is then chosen for the countable collection of sources and tests used in this proof. The countable core encodes limits and density classes after the uniform bounds have been established.

<a id="sec:edge-estimates"></a>
### Gaussian estimates at the bottom edge scales

The observation below reveals noisy information about leading spin projections. We control the variance of a bounded spin function left unresolved by that observation by $Cp^{-2}$ times its heat-bath energy, with a small remainder, at every scale for which $np^3$ exceeds a tight threshold. The exponent $2$ is important: a fixed relative covariance error at every scale would accumulate to a power loss. We first extend the Gaussian cap estimates to these scales and then show that the relative error is integrable with respect to $\mathrm d\log p$.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
#### Cap observations and the estimates

Throughout this section the disorder is Gaussian, with the independent GOE diagonal and randomized eigenvector signs specified in Section 2. Set $r_n=n^{-1/3+10^{-4}}$, the terminal scale of the source estimates, and write $d=2I-W$. Define, in physical coordinates, $$\begin{aligned}
 P_p&=U\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(\mathbf 1_{\{d_a\le p^2\}})U^{\mathsf T},&
 \mathcal H_p&=\operatorname{ran}P_p,\\
 B_p&=U\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}((p^2-d_a)_+)U^{\mathsf T},&
 W_p&=W-B_p,\\
 k_p&=np^3,&M_p&=\sqrt{np}.
\end{aligned}$$ Thus $p^2M_p^2=k_p$. A field at scale $p$ lies in $\mathcal H_p$, with length unit $p^2M_p$. For such a field let $$\phi_p(h)=\log\nu_n
 \exp\left(\tfrac12 X^{\mathsf T}W_pX+h^{\mathsf T}X\right),
 \qquad m_p(h)=\nabla\phi_p(h),\qquad
 K_p(h)=\left[P_p\nabla^2\phi_p(h)P_p\right]_{\mathcal H_p}.$$ Brackets with subscript $\mathcal H_p$ denote compression to that space. The probability with this log partition function is $\mu_{p,h}$. Thus $m_p$ and $K_p$ are its mean and its active covariance. Superscript ${\rm sp}$ denotes the same definitions with normalized surface measure on $\{X:\|X\|^2=n\}$ in place of $\nu_n$. In the tight-constant convention of Section <a href="#sec:background" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:background">2</a>, a tight lower threshold for $k_p$ means that, for each $\chi>0$, a deterministic threshold $K_\chi$ can be chosen on an event of limiting lower probability at least $1-\chi$.

For $X\sim\mu$, form the Gaussian observation <a id="edge:observation"></a>$$\label{edge:observation}
 h_p=B_pX+\beta_p,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\beta_p,\beta_q)=B_{\min(p,q)}.$$ One construction uses an independent scalar Brownian motion in spectral coordinate $a$, evaluated at $(p^2-d_a)_+$. Bayes’ formula gives $\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(X\mid h_q,\ q\le p)=\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(X\mid h_p)=\mu_{p,h_p}$ at fixed $W$. Write $Q_\mu$ for the joint law of the spin and all observations at fixed $W$. The observation filtration excludes the spin. The path $h_p$ is continuous at $p^2=d_a$; the new coordinate then has zero precision. The finitely many activation points may be omitted in scale integrals. For $0\le f\le1$, put <a id="edge:posterior-variance"></a>$$\label{edge:posterior-variance}
 F_p(h)=\mu_{p,h}[f],\qquad
 V_p(f)=Q_\mu[\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(f\mid h_p)].$$

<a id="edge:saddle"></a>
For $u>-p^2$ define $$R_{p,u}=U\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}\left((\max\{d_a,p^2\}+u)^{-1}\right)U^{\mathsf T}.$$ On the spectral events and scales used below, the spherical saddle $\alpha_p(h)>-p^2$ is the unique solution of $$\label{edge:saddle}
 n=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,\alpha_p(h)}+\|R_{p,\alpha_p(h)}h\|^2.$$ Existence, uniqueness, and bounds on this solution are proved below. Since $R_{p,u}$ is scalar on $\mathcal H_p$, the length of a field whose saddle is $u$ is <a id="edge:saddle-length"></a>$$\label{edge:saddle-length}
 \ell_p(u)=(p^2+u)\sqrt{n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,u}}$$ whenever the expression under the square root is nonnegative.

<a id="edge:haar-bias"></a>
<a id="edge:path-likelihood"></a>
<a id="edge:bias-transfer"></a>
We use one change of probability law, always conditional on a fixed spectrum. Under the ordinary law $U$ is Haar, and $Q_\mu$ is the joint law of the spin and its physical observations at the resulting $W$. With probability reference measures in the partition functions, set $L_\circ(U)=Z_{\rm cube}(W)/Z_{\rm sp}(W)$. Haar averaging gives $E_UL_\circ=1$. Under $\mathbf P$, first choose $U$ with Haar density $L_\circ$, and then use $Q_\mu$ given $W$; write $\mathbf E$ for its expectation. The spherical identity of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 2.5 and Equation (2.8)) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] gives $$\label{edge:haar-bias}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Law}}_{\mathbf P}(U^{\mathsf T}X)
   =\mu^{\rm sp}\text{ in spectral coordinates},\qquad
 E_U(L_\circ-1)^2=o(1)$$ on its retained eigenvalue events. Consequently the spectral observation path $(U^{\mathsf T}h_p)_p$ under $\mathbf P$ has the spherical observation law, denoted by $Q^{\rm sp}$. For comparison, let $\mathsf R$ choose $U$ with Haar law independently of a spectral path with law $Q^{\rm sp}$, and transport that path to physical coordinates by $U$. For the filtration generated by $U$ and observations through $p$, but not by $X$, the exact likelihood from (OpenAI 2026d, Equation (2.9)) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] is $$\label{edge:path-likelihood}
 \frac{\mathrm d\mathbf P}{\mathrm d\mathsf R}\bigg|_{\mathcal F_p}
 =L_p(h_p),\qquad
 L_p(h)=\exp\{\phi_p(h)-\phi_p^{\rm sp}(h)\}.$$ The notation $L_p(h)$ suppresses its dependence on $U$: in a Haar average the spectral field $U^{\mathsf T}h$ is held fixed, while $L_p(h)$ still varies with $U$. At every such field $E_UL_p(h)=1$. To check the likelihood, the observation density is a common Gaussian factor times the posterior partition function divided by the original one, and $L_\circ$ cancels the original partition functions. In particular, for every nonnegative spin or observation functional $G$, $$\label{edge:bias-transfer}
 E_U[\mathbf 1_{\{L_\circ\ge1/2\}}Q_\mu G]\le2\mathbf E G.$$

<a id="stmt-prop-edge-estimates"></a>
<div id="prop:edge-estimates" class="proposition">

<a id="edge:scale-range"></a>
**Proposition 3** (Cap estimates with a tight lower threshold). *Fix $0<C_1<\infty$, $0\le R<\infty$, positive tolerances $\epsilon_{\rm sp},\epsilon_0,\epsilon_v,\epsilon_g$, and $\zeta>0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are finite positive constants $K,C,c,a,v_0$, a width $s_0>0$, a radius $R_{\rm ann}<\infty$, and Gaussian disorder events $\mathcal C_n$ with $\liminf_n\mathbb P_{\rm GOE}(\mathcal C_n)\ge1-\varepsilon$, such that the following hold on $\mathcal C_n$, simultaneously at every scale $$\label{edge:scale-range}
 K\le k_p=np^3,\qquad p\le C_1r_n.$$*

<a id="edge:trace-estimates"></a>
1.  *The active dimension is between $ck_p$ and $Ck_p$, $d_1\ge-\epsilon_{\rm sp}p^2$, and, with $b_0=4/(3\pi)$, $$\label{edge:trace-estimates}
     \left|\frac{n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,0}}{np}-b_0\right|\le\epsilon_{\rm sp},
     \qquad
     \left|\frac p n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,0}^2-2b_0\right|\le\epsilon_{\rm sp}.$$ On $\|h\|\le Rp^2M_p$, the saddle satisfies $-1+c_R\le\alpha_p(h)/p^2\le C_R$. On $|u|\le s_0p^2$, $\ell_p(u)\asymp p^2M_p$ and $\ell'_p(u)\asymp M_p$.*

<a id="edge:static-estimates"></a>
2.  *On the field ball $\|h\|\le Rp^2M_p$, $$\label{edge:static-estimates}
     \begin{split}
     K_p(h)&\preceq C_Rp^{-2}I_{\mathcal H_p},\\
     |\phi_p(h)-\phi_p^{\rm sp}(h)|&\le\epsilon_v k_p,\\
     \|P_pm_p(h)-R_{p,\alpha_p(h)}h\|&\le\epsilon_gM_p .
     \end{split}$$ The constant $C_R$ in the first line may be chosen independently of the requested annular tolerance $\epsilon_0$. On the full annulus $|\alpha_p(h)|\le s_0p^2$, the field is nonzero; for $e=h/\|h\|$, <a id="edge:coarse-curvature"></a>$$\label{edge:coarse-curvature}
     K_p(h)\preceq(1+\epsilon_0)p^{-2}I_{\mathcal H_p},
     \qquad p^2\langle e,K_p(h)e\rangle\le0.9 .$$ The annulus lies in $\|h\|\le R_{\rm ann}p^2M_p$, and the event also includes the static comparisons on this ball, with constants allowed to depend on $R_{\rm ann}$.*

<a id="edge:projection-tails"></a>
<a id="edge:ordinary-annulus"></a>
3.  *For every $v\ge v_0$, the uncapped law $\mu$, every posterior $\mu_{p,h}$ in the stated field ball, and their spherical counterparts satisfy $$\label{edge:projection-tails}
     \Pr\{\|P_pX\|>vM_p\}\le C e^{-c k_pv^6}.$$ The event is empty for $v>p^{-1/2}$. The spherical pair bound of Lemma <a href="#edge:spherical-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spherical-tails">6</a> also holds for each number of replicas fixed in advance, with constants allowed to depend on that number. Moreover, $$\label{edge:ordinary-annulus}
     Q_\mu\{|\alpha_p(h_p)|>\zeta p^2\}\le C e^{-c k_p}.$$*

<a id="edge:variance-estimates"></a>
4.  *For every scale in <a href="#edge:scale-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:scale-range">[edge:scale-range]</a> with $p\le r_n$, simultaneously for every $0\le f\le1$, $$\label{edge:variance-estimates}
     \begin{split}
     V_p(f)&\le Cp^{-2}\mathcal E(f)+C e^{-c k_p^a},\\
     p^2Q_\mu\|\nabla_{\mathcal H_p}F_p(h_p)\|^2
           &\le C V_p(f)+C e^{-c k_p^a}.
     \end{split}$$ The event and constants in these inequalities are independent of $f$.*

*All constants in the saddle, length, and comparison bounds are deterministic on $\mathcal C_n$ and may depend on the fixed inputs and the requested failure probability, but not on $n$, $p$, or the field in its stated region.*

</div>

Every radius, tolerance, and finite multiplicative enlargement of a scale interval is fixed before the constants are chosen. Increasing $K$ by a fixed factor supplies any such enlargement at the lower endpoint. A finite number of further requests for cap estimates may be imposed by intersecting their events, with a smaller failure probability assigned to each. This preserves the constants and exponent of any variance estimate already obtained.

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
###### Reduction to positive covariance error.

<a id="edge:variance-identity"></a>
Fix $W$ and $0\le f\le1$. In the time variable $t=p^2$, let $$\mathcal F_t^{\rm obs}=\sigma(h_q:0\le q\le\sqrt t),
 \qquad M_t^f=F_{\sqrt t}(h_{\sqrt t}).$$ This filtration excludes the spin and includes any information in $h_0$; the initial precision $B_0$ need not vanish. The bounded posterior martingale $M^f$ is continuous. On positive time intervals, its predictable bracket has density $\|\nabla_{\mathcal H_{\sqrt t}}F_{\sqrt t}(h_{\sqrt t})\|^2$. The coefficient can change at an activation, but the martingale has no jump there. Total variance and the bracket identity therefore give $$\label{edge:variance-identity}
 -\frac{\mathrm dV_p(f)}{\mathrm d(p^2)}
       =Q_\mu\|\nabla_{\mathcal H_p}F_p(h_p)\|^2$$ almost everywhere in $p>0$, and in integrated form across activation points. This is the localization variance calculation in (Eldan, Koehler, and Zeitouni 2022, proof of Theorem 1, Equation (14) and the display after Equation (15)) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[EldanKoehlerZeitouni2022](#ref-EldanKoehlerZeitouni2022)], with deterministic rate $P_p$.

<a id="edge:common-failure-cost"></a>
<a id="edge:gradient-bounds"></a>
<a id="edge:variance-amplification"></a>
Let $\mathcal N$ be a jointly measurable set of triples $(p,W,h)$ with $h\in\mathcal H_p$, chosen independently of $f$, and let $\eta_p=\eta_p(W)\ge0$ be a measurable scalar fixed at each $(W,p)$. Suppose that $p^2K_p(h)\preceq(1+\eta_p)I_{\mathcal H_p}$ for $h\in\mathcal H_p$ when $(p,W,h)\notin\mathcal N$. Put $$\label{edge:common-failure-cost}
 Z_p(X)=\frac{\|P_pX\|^2}{M_p^2},\qquad
 \rho_p(W)=k_pQ_\mu\!\left[
       \mathbf 1_{\mathcal N}(p,W,h_p)\mu_{p,h_p}(Z_p)\right].$$ Conditional covariance and Cauchy–Schwarz give, at the observed field, $$\label{edge:gradient-bounds}
 \begin{split}
 \|\nabla_{\mathcal H_p}F_p(h_p)\|^2
       &\le\|K_p(h_p)\|\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_{\mu_{p,h_p}}(f),\\
 p^2\|\nabla_{\mathcal H_p}F_p(h_p)\|^2
       &\le k_p\mu_{p,h_p}(Z_p).
 \end{split}$$ For the second bound, write $\nabla F_p=\mu_{p,h_p}[P_pX(f-F_p)]$ and use $|f-F_p|\le1$. Its right side is a common cost for every such $f$. Splitting the expectation in <a href="#edge:variance-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:variance-identity">[edge:variance-identity]</a> at $\mathcal N$ yields <a id="edge:variance-differential"></a>$$\label{edge:variance-differential}
 -\frac{\mathrm dV_p}{\mathrm d\log p}
       \le2(1+\eta_p)V_p+2\rho_p$$ almost everywhere. If $\eta_u\le Ck_u^{-a}$ for a fixed $a>0$ on $[p,q]$, its backward integrating factor is at most $$\exp\left(2\int_p^q(1+Ck_u^{-a})\,\mathrm d\log u\right)
       \le C(q/p)^2,\qquad
 \int_p^qk_u^{-a}\,\mathrm d\log u
       =\frac{k_p^{-a}-k_q^{-a}}{3a}\le\frac{K^{-a}}{3a}$$ whenever $k_p\ge K$. In particular, $$\label{edge:variance-amplification}
 V_p\le C(q/p)^2V_q+
       C\int_p^q(u/p)^2\rho_u\,\mathrm d\log u .$$ The remaining work for Item 4 is to obtain this covariance bound with $\eta_p=Ck_p^{-a}$, control the common cost $\rho_p$ on dyadic intervals, and use the source variance estimate at $r_n$. The integrable relative error is what preserves the exponent $2$.

<a id="pm-h-13"></a>
#### Spectral counts, saddles, and spherical tails

<a id="edge:threshold-convention"></a>
For a specified spectral error, being small above a tight threshold means $$\label{edge:threshold-convention}
 \lim_{K\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \mathbb P_{\rm GOE}\left\{
 \sup_{\substack{np^3\ge K\\p\le C_1r_n}}
       \text{the specified error at \(p\)}>\eta\right\}=0
 \quad(\eta>0).$$ Only finitely many errors at a time are needed. This is a double-limit assertion, not convergence with $n$ at a fixed $K$.

<a id="stmt-edge-spectral"></a>
<div id="edge:spectral" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:counting-tail"></a>
<a id="edge:global-spectral"></a>
**Lemma 4** (Spectral estimates above a tight threshold). *In the convention <a href="#edge:threshold-convention" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:threshold-convention">[edge:threshold-convention]</a>, the measures $\nu_p=k_p^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{d_i/p^2}$ converge on fixed bounded intervals to $\pi^{-1}\sqrt v\,\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}}\mathrm dv$. Their distribution functions converge uniformly on compact intervals. The same convention gives $d_1/p^2\ge-o(1)$, $\dim\mathcal H_p/k_p\to2/(3\pi)$, and the two limits in <a href="#edge:trace-estimates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:trace-estimates">[edge:trace-estimates]</a>. On spectral events of arbitrarily large limiting probability there is also a fixed $C$ such that $$\label{edge:counting-tail}
 \begin{aligned}
 \#\{i:d_i\le u\}&\le Cnu^{3/2}
       &&(u\ge cp^2,\ u\le4),\\
 \int_{[A,\infty)}(1+v)^{-2}\nu_p(\mathrm dv)&\le CA^{-1/2}
       &&(A\ge1),
 \end{aligned}$$ for every fixed $c>0$, after increasing the threshold. Every spectral restriction below also includes eigenvalue-only events $\mathcal S_n^{\rm glob}$ of probability $1-o(1)$ on which, uniformly over their spectra, $$\label{edge:global-spectral}
 \frac1n\sum_i\delta_{\lambda_i}\ \Longrightarrow\
 \rho_{\rm sc}(\,\mathrm dx):=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,
             \mathbf 1_{\{|x|\le2\}}\,\mathrm dx,\qquad
 \lambda_1\longrightarrow2,\qquad \|W\|\le3 .$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-spectral"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-spectral</summary>

<a id="edge:source-resolvents"></a>
*Proof.* We use the eigenvalue-only event of (OpenAI 2026c, Proposition 3.1) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[CS](#ref-CS)]. For every deterministic $L_n\to\infty$ with $L_n\le\log n$, that proposition gives positive denominators and, uniformly for $L_nn^{-2/3}\le u\le M$ with fixed $M$, $$\label{edge:source-resolvents}
 \begin{split}
 m_1(u):=\frac1n\sum_i(d_i+u)^{-1}
  &=\frac{2+u-\sqrt{u(4+u)}}2+o(\sqrt u),\\
 m_2(u):=\frac1n\sum_i(d_i+u)^{-2}
  &\le C_Mu^{-1/2},\\
 \lambda_j&=2+o(L_nn^{-2/3})\quad(1\le j\le3),
 \qquad \|W\|\le3 .
 \end{split}$$ The errors have deterministic uniform bounds on an event of probability at least $1-Ce^{-cL_n^{1/4}}$.

For <a href="#edge:global-spectral" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:global-spectral">[edge:global-spectral]</a>, take $\mathcal S_n^{\rm glob}$ to be the separate source event with $L_n=\sqrt{\log n}$. Its probability tends to one, and the edge and norm assertions follow directly from <a href="#edge:source-resolvents" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:source-resolvents">[edge:source-resolvents]</a>. For every fixed $u>1$, the first resolvent converges uniformly there to $$\frac{2+u-\sqrt{u(4+u)}}2
 =\int\frac{\rho_{\rm sc}(\,\mathrm dx)}{2+u-x}.$$ The norm bound makes the empirical spectral measures a compact family. Every weak subsequential limit therefore has the displayed transform for every $u>1$, and uniqueness of the Stieltjes transform identifies it with $\rho_{\rm sc}$. A contradiction by subsequences gives this weak convergence uniformly over the source event. Intersecting with this event does not change the tight-threshold convention.

Let $K_n\to\infty$ be arbitrary and set $L_n=\min\{K_n^{1/3},\sqrt{\log n}\}$, changing finitely many initial values if necessary. For $np^3\ge K_n$, $L_nn^{-2/3}=o(p^2)$. Thus, for every fixed $v>0$, $$m_1(vp^2)=1-\sqrt v\,p+O_v(p^2)+o_v(p)$$ uniformly in the scale range, and $d_1/p^2\ge-o(1)$. For $u\ge cp^2$, the counted denominators satisfy $0<d_i+u\le2u$. Consequently $$\#\{d_i\le u\}\le4u^2\sum_i(d_i+u)^{-2}\le Cnu^{3/2}.$$ Summing on dyadic bands gives the second bound in <a href="#edge:counting-tail" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:counting-tail">[edge:counting-tail]</a>; the last band above $u=4$ costs $O(p)$ by $\|W\|\le3$, and obeys the same bound.

<a id="edge:transform-difference"></a>
For fixed $v,w>0$, the transform difference is exactly $$\label{edge:transform-difference}
 \int\left(\frac1{x+v}-\frac1{x+w}\right)\nu_p(\mathrm dx)
 =\frac{m_1(vp^2)-m_1(wp^2)}p
 \longrightarrow\sqrt w-\sqrt v.$$ To identify the limit including the tail, put $\omega_p(\mathrm dx)=(1+x)^{-2}\nu_p(\mathrm dx)$. These finite measures have bounded mass, the tail bound <a href="#edge:counting-tail" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:counting-tail">[edge:counting-tail]</a>, and negative support in an interval shrinking to zero. Every weak limit $\omega$ is therefore supported on $[0,\infty)$. Taking $w=1$ in <a href="#edge:transform-difference" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:transform-difference">[edge:transform-difference]</a> gives $$\int\frac{1+x}{x+v}\,\omega(\mathrm dx)=\frac1{1+\sqrt v}.$$ Letting $v\to1$ gives $\omega([0,\infty))=1/2$, and hence $$\int\frac{\omega(\mathrm dx)}{x+v}
       =\frac1{2(1+\sqrt v)^2}.$$ Uniqueness of the Stieltjes transform identifies $\omega(\mathrm dx)=\pi^{-1}\sqrt x(1+x)^{-2}\mathrm dx$. The continuous distribution function of the corresponding limit of $\nu_p$ gives uniformity in endpoints on compact intervals. Failure of uniformity over $p$ would provide a sequence of scales to which this same compactness argument applies, a contradiction.

The clipped second trace has limit $$\frac p n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,0}^2
 =\int(\max\{x,1\})^{-2}\nu_p(\mathrm dx)
 \longrightarrow
 \frac1\pi\left(\int_0^1\sqrt x\,\mathrm dx+
                 \int_1^\infty x^{-3/2}\,\mathrm dx\right)
 =\frac8{3\pi}.$$ For the first trace, subtract an ordinary resolvent before integrating: $$\frac{n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,0}}{np}
 =\frac{1-m_1(p^2)}p+
 \int\left(\frac1{x+1}-\frac1{\max\{x,1\}}\right)\nu_p(\mathrm dx)
 \longrightarrow\frac4{3\pi}.$$ The difference kernel is $O(x^{-2})$. Its limiting integral is $4/(3\pi)-1$, obtained by substituting $x=t^2$ on each of $(0,1)$ and $(1,\infty)$.

These assertions hold for every arbitrarily slowly divergent $K_n$. If <a href="#edge:threshold-convention" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:threshold-convention">[edge:threshold-convention]</a> failed, one could choose $K_j\to\infty$ and $n_j\to\infty$ with failure probability bounded away from zero and embed $K_{n_j}=K_j$ in a divergent deterministic sequence. The preceding uniform conclusion contradicts that subsequence. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-norm-density"></a>
<div id="edge:norm-density" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5** (Saddles and squared-norm densities). *On the spectral restrictions of Lemma <a href="#edge:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spectral">4</a>, the saddle and length conclusions in Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a> hold. For a saddle field in a fixed ball let $$Y\sim N(m,\widehat R),\qquad \widehat R=R_{p,\alpha_p(h)},\quad m=\widehat Rh,\quad
 \sigma^2=2\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\widehat R^2+4m^{\mathsf T}\widehat Rm.$$ Then $\sigma^2\asymp n/p$, and the density $f_Y$ of $\|Y\|^2$ satisfies $f_Y(n)\asymp\sqrt{p/n}=p^2/\sqrt{k_p}$. In standard-deviation units this density converges uniformly on $\mathbb R$ to the standard normal density as $K\to\infty$.*

<a id="edge:replica-norm-density"></a>
*For a fixed number $m_0$ of replicas, suppose the spectral rows $Y_i\in\mathbb R^{m_0}$ are independent Gaussian vectors and at least $L>2$ row covariances obey $cu^{-1}I_{m_0}\preceq C_i\preceq Cu^{-1}I_{m_0}$. Their means are arbitrary. The joint density of $\mathcal Q=(\sum_iY_{i1}^2,\ldots,\sum_iY_{im_0}^2)$ obeys $$\label{edge:replica-norm-density}
 \sup_z f_{\mathcal Q}(z)\le C_{m_0}(u/\sqrt L)^{m_0}.$$ This applies after rowwise Gaussian tilts which preserve the stated band and independence of the rows.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-norm-density"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-norm-density</summary>

<a id="edge:scaled-saddle"></a>
*Proof.* Put $t=u/p^2$ and $\mathfrak d_p(t)=(n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,tp^2})/(np)$. For $y=\|h\|/(p^2M_p)$, the saddle equation becomes $$\label{edge:scaled-saddle}
 \mathfrak d_p(t)=\frac{y^2}{(1+t)^2},\qquad t>-1,\qquad
 \mathfrak d'_p(t)=\frac p n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,tp^2}^2.$$ Lemma <a href="#edge:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spectral">4</a> gives $\mathfrak d_p(0)$ arbitrarily close to $b_0$, and $$\mathfrak d'_p(t)\ge
       \frac{\dim\mathcal H_p/k_p}{(1+t)^2}.$$ It follows by integration that $\mathfrak d_p(-1+\kappa)<0$ for a sufficiently small fixed $\kappa>0$; no saddle can lie there or below. On $t\ge0$, $\mathfrak d_p(t)\ge b_0/2$, so <a href="#edge:scaled-saddle" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:scaled-saddle">[edge:scaled-saddle]</a> bounds $t$ above when $y\le R$. The right side of <a href="#edge:saddle" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:saddle">[edge:saddle]</a>, viewed as a function of its parameter, is strictly decreasing and continuous, tends to infinity at $-p^2$, and tends to zero at infinity. This also proves existence and uniqueness. Denominator comparison gives $\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\widehat R^2\asymp n/p$, $\|m\|^2\le C_Rnp$, and $\|\widehat R\|\le C_Rp^{-2}$, hence $\sigma^2\asymp n/p$. For a sufficiently small fixed $s_0$, both $\mathfrak d_p(t)$ and $\mathfrak d'_p(t)$ are bounded above and below on $|t|\le s_0$. Differentiating $\ell_p(tp^2)=p^2M_p(1+t)\sqrt{\mathfrak d_p(t)}$ proves the length and derivative bounds.

<a id="edge:norm-characteristic"></a>
<a id="edge:norm-expansion"></a>
<a id="edge:norm-local-limit"></a>
We record the density argument used here and later. For independent $Y_i=a_i+\sqrt{\upsilon_i}G_i$, suppose $$\max_i\upsilon_i\le Cp^{-2},\qquad
 \sigma^2:=2\sum_i\upsilon_i^2+4\sum_i\upsilon_i a_i^2
       \asymp k_pp^{-4},$$ and at least $ck_p$ variances are at least $cp^{-2}$. The Gaussian quadratic formula, as in (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.3, Equation (15.5)) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)], gives $$\label{edge:norm-characteristic}
 \left|\mathbb Ee^{it\sum_iY_i^2}\right|
 =\prod_i(1+4t^2\upsilon_i^2)^{-1/4}
   \exp\left(-\sum_i
       \frac{2t^2\upsilon_i a_i^2}{1+4t^2\upsilon_i^2}\right).$$ Expansion of the centered log characteristic function through order two gives $$\label{edge:norm-expansion}
 \log\mathbb Ee^{it(\|Y\|^2-\mathbb E\|Y\|^2)/\sigma}
       =-t^2/2+O(k_p^{-1/2}|t|^3)
       \quad (|t|\le c\sqrt{k_p}).$$ Indeed its remainder is at most $$C|t/\sigma|^3\sum_i(\upsilon_i^3+\upsilon_i^2a_i^2)
       \le Ck_p^{-1/2}|t|^3.$$ The band in <a href="#edge:norm-characteristic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:norm-characteristic">[edge:norm-characteristic]</a> bounds the modulus in these units by $(1+ct^2/k_p)^{-c'k_p}$. Its real logarithm is at most $-c_0t^2$ up to a small fixed multiple of $\sqrt{k_p}$, and its integral outside that interval is exponentially small in $k_p$. Fourier inversion and <a href="#edge:norm-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:norm-expansion">[edge:norm-expansion]</a> give $$\label{edge:norm-local-limit}
 \sup_z\left|\sigma f_Y(\mathbb E\|Y\|^2+\sigma z)
       -(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/2}\right|\le Ck_p^{-1/2}.$$ At the saddle $\mathbb E\|Y\|^2=n$, proving the lower and upper density bounds. At any mean, the same characteristic majorant gives the upper bound $Cp^2/\sqrt{k_p}$.

For replicas let $T_t=\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(t_1,\ldots,t_{m_0})$ and $H_i=C_i^{1/2}T_tC_i^{1/2}$. The modulus of the row characteristic function is at most $\det(I+4H_i^2)^{-1/4}$; its extra factor from a nonzero mean is at most one. The singular values of $H_i$ are at least $cu^{-1}$ times those of $T_t$, including when the entries of $T_t$ have different signs. Independence of the $L$ rows bounds the joint characteristic function by $\prod_j(1+ct_j^2/u^2)^{-L/4}$. Its integral proves <a href="#edge:replica-norm-density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:replica-norm-density">[edge:replica-norm-density]</a>. This is the argument of (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.3, Equation (15.6)) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)]; it explains the independence requirement on the spectral rows. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-spherical-tails"></a>
<div id="edge:spherical-tails" class="lemma">

**Lemma 6** (Spherical projection and pair tails). *Fix a field radius and a fixed number of replicas. On the spectral restrictions above, for every $p$ with $k_p\ge K$ and $p\le C_1r_n$, both the uncapped zero-field spherical law and the capped spherical law at a field in that ball satisfy <a id="edge:spherical-tail-bounds"></a>$$\label{edge:spherical-tail-bounds}
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{\|P_pX\|>vM_p\}&\le C e^{-c k_pv^6}
       &&(v\ge v_0),\\
 \Pr\{|n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X'|>w\}&\le C e^{-c n w^3}
       &&(Cp\le w\le\rho_0).
 \end{aligned}$$ Here $X,X'$ are independent replicas at the same field, $\rho_0>0$ is fixed and small, and the second bound holds for every pair of a fixed finite family. The constants are uniform in $p,n$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-spherical-tails"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-spherical-tails</summary>

<a id="edge:frozen-density"></a>
<a id="edge:frozen-normalizer-cost"></a>
*Proof.* We give the scale check in the polar argument of (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.3, Equations (15.5)–(15.8)) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)]. For an interaction $A$, write $R_{A,u}=(2+u-A)^{-1}$ and $$q_{A,u}(h)=c_n+\tfrac n2(2+u)+\tfrac12\log\det R_{A,u}
                      +\tfrac12h^{\mathsf T}R_{A,u}h,\qquad
 c_n=\log\!\left(2^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)n^{1-n/2}\right).$$ Coarea in squared radius gives, exactly, $$\label{edge:frozen-density}
 \phi_A^{\rm sp}(h)=q_{A,u}(h)+\log f_{A,u,h}(n),\qquad
 \partial_uq_{A,u}(h)
   =\tfrac12\bigl(n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{A,u}-\|R_{A,u}h\|^2\bigr),$$ where $f_{A,u,h}$ is the density of $\|N(R_{A,u}h,R_{A,u})\|^2$. In the capped case take $A=W_p$ and start at its saddle $u=\alpha$. For $u\ge p^2$, $$n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,u}
 \le Cn\sqrt u+Ck_pp^2/u^2\le Cn\sqrt u.$$ The first term is <a href="#edge:source-resolvents" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:source-resolvents">[edge:source-resolvents]</a>; the second compares the clipped active denominators with $d_i+u$, using $\dim\mathcal H_p\le Ck_p$. For $u$ in a bounded range in $p^2$ units, the upper bound is $C_Rnp$. Integrating <a href="#edge:frozen-density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:frozen-density">[edge:frozen-density]</a> yields $$\label{edge:frozen-normalizer-cost}
 q_{W_p,u}(h)-q_{W_p,\alpha}(h)\le Cnu^{3/2}+C_Rk_p,$$ where the first constant is independent of the field radius.

<a id="edge:polar-tail"></a>
For a rowwise quadratic test $\mathcal T$ of $m_0$ replicas and $\lambda>0$, let $f_{\mathcal Q}^{u,\lambda}$ be the norm density under the normalized Gaussian tilt $e^{\lambda\mathcal T}$ of $m_0$ independent copies of $N(R_{p,u}h,R_{p,u})$. Exponential Markov and polar coarea give $$\label{edge:polar-tail}
 \begin{split}
 (\mu_{p,h}^{\rm sp})^{\otimes m_0}\{\mathcal T\ge b\}
