 \le{}&
 e^{m_0(q_{W_p,u}(h)-q_{W_p,\alpha}(h))-\lambda b}
 \mathbb E_u e^{\lambda\mathcal T}
 \frac{f_{\mathcal Q}^{u,\lambda}(n\mathbf1)}
      {f_{W_p,\alpha,h}(n)^{m_0}} .
 \end{split}$$ This compares norm densities before and after the normalized tilt; it does not divide by the probability of a shrinking shell.

For a pair take $\mathcal T=\pm X^{\mathsf T}X'$, $b=nw$, $u=\iota w^2$, and $\lambda=c'u$, with $c'>0$ a sufficiently small absolute constant. We will choose $\iota>0$ small and then the lower multiple of $w/p$ large, so that $u\gg p^2$. The Gaussian formula gives <a id="edge:quadratic-mgf"></a>$$\label{edge:quadratic-mgf}
 \log\mathbb E_u e^{\lambda\mathcal T}
 \le C\lambda^2\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,u}^2+C\lambda\|R_{p,u}h\|^2
 \le Cnu^{3/2}+C_Rk_p.$$ Indeed $\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,u}^2\le Cn/\sqrt u$ and $\|R_{p,u}h\|^2\le C_Rnp^5/u^2$; the pair quadratic has zero first trace in the centered Gaussian formula. For $\mathcal T=\|P_pX\|^2$, $b=nw$, its extra first trace costs only $Ck_p$. The choice of $c'$ preserves positive precision and covariance comparable to $u^{-1}I_{m_0}$ on $ck_p$ active rows. Lemma <a href="#edge:norm-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:norm-density">5</a> bounds the density ratio in <a href="#edge:polar-tail" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:polar-tail">[edge:polar-tail]</a> by $C_{m_0}(u/p^2)^{m_0}$.

For uncapped zero field start at $u=p^2$. The resolvent gives $n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}(d+p^2)^{-1}\asymp np$, a leading variance comparable to $p^{-2}$, and variance $O(n/p)$ for the other squares. Chebyshev’s inequality puts the residual squared length to be supplied by that coordinate in $[cnp,Cnp]$ with probability $1-C/k_p$. On this interval its Gaussian-square density is at least $c\sqrt{p/n}e^{-Ck_p}$. Convolution gives the same lower density scale, with this extra exponential factor. The uncapped resolvent also gives <a href="#edge:frozen-normalizer-cost" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:frozen-normalizer-cost">[edge:frozen-normalizer-cost]</a>, and the tilted upper density has the same band bound.

The logarithm of the resulting probability is at most $$-c'\iota nw^3+C\iota^{3/2}nw^3+C_Rk_p
       +O_{m_0}(\log(u/p^2)).$$ Choose $\iota$ so that $C\sqrt\iota<c'/4$, and then $w/p$ larger than a sufficiently large fixed constant. Since $nw^3=k_p(w/p)^3$, the last two terms are absorbed by another $c'\iota nw^3/4$ when $K$ is large. This proves the pair bound. For projection put $w=v^2p\le1$; then $nw^3=k_pv^6$. For $v>p^{-1/2}$ the event is empty because $\|X\|=\sqrt n$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-limit-growth"></a>
<div id="edge:limit-growth" class="corollary">

**Corollary 7** (Growth of the limiting spectral rates). *For GOE-almost every $g$, and every $b$ with $b+g_1>0$, there are finite positive constants $c_{g,b},C_{g,b}$ such that <a id="edge:limit-rate-bounds"></a>$$\label{edge:limit-rate-bounds}
 c_{g,b}(1+i)^{2/3}\le g_i+b\le C_{g,b}(1+i)^{2/3}
 \qquad(i\ge1).$$ They can be chosen measurably when $b$ is a measurable admissible function of $g$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-limit-growth"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-limit-growth</summary>

*Proof.* Fix errors in Lemma <a href="#edge:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spectral">4</a> for which the number of points with $d_i\le p^2$ is between $c np^3$ and $Cnp^3$, and apply it at the countable scales $np^3=2^jK$. For any finite list, finite edge-coordinate convergence transfers the inequalities, with slightly enlarged constants, to counts of limiting points below $(2^jK)^{2/3}$. A fixed small buffer in the endpoints may be used; the limiting process has no point at any of these countably many fixed endpoints. Increase the finite list and use continuity of probability for decreasing events. The uniform finite-$n$ event shows that all the limiting inequalities hold with probability arbitrarily close to one when $K$ is large. Letting that failure probability tend to zero shows that almost surely, after a finite threshold, $$cL^{3/2}\le\#\{i:g_i\le L\}\le CL^{3/2}$$ on dyadic $L$, and hence on all large $L$ by monotonicity. Invert these inequalities, add $b$, and adjust the bounds for the finitely many remaining positive numbers $g_i+b$. The least integer threshold and rational bounds give measurable choices. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-14"></a>
#### Comparison with the cube

The spherical estimates control deterministic fields. We next obtain one disorder event on which the corresponding cube estimates hold for every field and scale. The additional work is confined to $k_p=O(\sqrt{\log n})$.

<a id="stmt-edge-gram-cell"></a>
<div id="edge:gram-cell" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:pair-cell-mass"></a>
<a id="edge:pair-cell-weighted"></a>
**Lemma 8** (Two-replica overlap cells). *Let $\mathcal{R}_n=\{-1+2j/n:0\le j\le n\}$ and $I_r=[r-1/n,r+1/n]$. The overlap of two independent uniform cube spins has mass $$p_n(r)=2^{-n}\binom{n}{n(1+r)/2},\qquad r\in\mathcal{R}_n,$$ whereas the overlap of two independent uniform spherical spins has density $$f_n(s)=\frac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma((n-1)/2)}
             (1-s^2)^{(n-3)/2},\qquad -1<s<1.$$ For a sufficiently small fixed $\rho_0>0$, uniformly for large $n$ and $r\in\mathcal{R}_n$ with $|r|\le\rho_0$, $$\label{edge:pair-cell-mass}
 p_n(r)\le e^{C+Cnr^4}\int_{I_r}f_n(s)\,\mathrm ds.$$ Let $H_2$ be the uniform law of an ordered orthonormal pair $(q,q')$. If a positive measurable angular weight $a_n(s,q,q')$ has finite integrals and satisfies, for $H_2$-almost every frame, $$|\log a_n(s,q,q')-\log a_n(r,q,q')|\le K_0
 \quad\text{for almost every }s\in I_r,$$ then $$\label{edge:pair-cell-weighted}
 p_n(r)\int a_n(r,q,q')\,\mathrm dH_2
 \le e^{C+Cnr^4+K_0}
       \int_{I_r}\!\int a_n(s,q,q')\,\mathrm dH_2\,f_n(s)\,\mathrm ds.$$ The cells have disjoint interiors. Summing over their midpoints in an overlap interval enlarges the spherical interval by at most $1/n$ at each endpoint.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-gram-cell"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-gram-cell</summary>

*Proof.* We derive this form for cells centered at lattice points from the two-replica calculations in (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.4, Equation (15.10)) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)] and (OpenAI 2026d, proof of Lemma 3.2) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. Set $$I(r)=\tfrac12\bigl((1+r)\log(1+r)+(1-r)\log(1-r)\bigr),
 \qquad J(r)=-\tfrac12\log(1-r^2).$$ Uniform Stirling bounds on $|r|\le\rho_0$ put $p_n(r)$ between fixed multiples of $n^{-1/2}e^{-nI(r)}$. The same bounds for the gamma ratio, and the bounded logarithmic oscillation of $f_n$ on $I_r$, put its cell integral between fixed multiples of $n^{-1/2}e^{-nJ(r)}$. Since $J(r)-I(r)=O(r^4)$, this proves <a href="#edge:pair-cell-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:pair-cell-mass">[edge:pair-cell-mass]</a>. The assumed oscillation of the positive angular weight gives <a href="#edge:pair-cell-weighted" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:pair-cell-weighted">[edge:pair-cell-weighted]</a> by integration. The final assertion follows directly from the cell endpoints. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-replica-comparison"></a>
<div id="edge:replica-comparison" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:likelihood-second-moment"></a>
**Lemma 9** (A Haar second moment at the low scales). *On the spectral restrictions above, for every fixed spectral field in a prescribed ball and every $K\le k_p$, $p\le C_1r_n$, $$\label{edge:likelihood-second-moment}
 E_U(L_p(h)-1)^2\le C_Rn^{-1/4}.$$ The field is fixed inside the expectation; the constant is uniform over the indicated fields and scales.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-replica-comparison"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-replica-comparison</summary>

<a id="edge:pair-angular-exponent"></a>
*Proof.* We adapt the two-replica calculation of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 3.2, Equations (3.3)–(3.4)) <a id="pm-cite-35"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)], whose stated observation range starts at $r_n$. The estimate below the source range is proved here. Conditional on $\rho=n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X'$, the Haar angular integral for a cube pair is the spherical angular integral. On the ordered orthonormal sum-and-difference frame $(q,q')$, its exponent is $$\label{edge:pair-angular-exponent}
 \Psi_{p,h}(s;q,q')=
 \frac n2\bigl((1+s)q^{\mathsf T}W_pq
       +(1-s){q'}^{\mathsf T}W_pq'\bigr)
       +\sqrt{2n(1+s)}\,h^{\mathsf T}q.$$ On a fixed $|s|\le2\rho_0<1$, the spectral norm bound and the field bound $\|h\|\le R\sqrt n\,p^{5/2}$ give $|\partial_s\Psi_{p,h}|\le C_Rn$. Thus the positive angular weight $e^{\Psi_{p,h}}$ has a fixed logarithmic oscillation on every width-$2/n$ cell, as required in <a href="#edge:pair-cell-weighted" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:pair-cell-weighted">[edge:pair-cell-weighted]</a>. Retain $|\rho|\le C'r_n$, choosing $C'$ larger than the lower tail constant in Lemma <a href="#edge:spherical-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spherical-tails">6</a> times $C_1$. On dyadic bands between $C'r_n$ and a small fixed $\rho_0$, the weighted cell comparison costs $e^{C+Cn\rho^4}$, while Lemma <a href="#edge:spherical-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spherical-tails">6</a> gives $Ce^{-cn\rho^3}$. The spherical band endpoints move by at most $1/n$, negligible compared with $r_n$. Decreasing $\rho_0$ makes the latter pay the former and leaves $Ce^{-cnr_n^3}$. At overlaps bounded away from zero, the global spectral law, edge limit, and norm bound in <a href="#edge:global-spectral" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:global-spectral">[edge:global-spectral]</a> supply the global inputs for the uncapped zero-field angular comparison of (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.4) <a id="pm-cite-36"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)]. Indeed, for every fixed $w>2$, they give $$\frac1n\log\det(wI-W)\longrightarrow
       \int\log(w-x)\rho_{\rm sc}(\,\mathrm dx);$$ interlacing gives the same per-site limit for every orthogonal-hyperplane compression. The cited deficit-filling lower bound then gives the full critical free-energy normalization by taking $n\to\infty$ at fixed $w>2$, followed by $w\downarrow2$. For clarity, the normalized zero-field contribution being bounded is $$\mathcal M_n(\rho_0;\boldsymbol\lambda)
   =E_U\!\left[L_\circ^2\,
       \mu_W^{\otimes2}\{|n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X'|\ge\rho_0\}\right].$$ Here $\boldsymbol\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)$ is fixed, $W=U\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(\boldsymbol\lambda)U^{\mathsf T}$, and $\mu_W$ is the zero-field cube Gibbs law for this $W$. The comparison in (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 15.4, “Zero field and overlaps bounded away from zero”) <a id="pm-cite-37"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)], together with the lower normalization in its Section 15.3, gives $\mathcal M_n(\rho_0;\boldsymbol\lambda)\le
\exp\{-\kappa_{\rho_0}n+o(n)\}$ for a fixed $\kappa_{\rho_0}>0$, along the retained spectral sequences with the preceding per-site errors uniform. This is a consequence of that proof; the norm bound supplies continuity at the endpoints. Changing to $W_p,h$ changes weights and log normalizers by $O_R(np^2+np^{5/2})=o(n)$, so that region still contributes $e^{-cn}$.

On retained cells of width $2/n$, Stirling’s formula for the binomial overlap mass and the spherical density proportional to $(1-\rho^2)^{(n-3)/2}$ gives relative error <a id="edge:retained-stirling"></a>$$\label{edge:retained-stirling}
 O(nr_n^4+r_n+n^{-1}).$$ This is the cell estimate in the cited replica proof, now with cutoff $C'r_n$ at every $p$. More precisely than the fixed bound above, the oscillation of <a href="#edge:pair-angular-exponent" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:pair-angular-exponent">[edge:pair-angular-exponent]</a> on one cell is at most $$C\bigl(|q^{\mathsf T}W_pq-{q'}^{\mathsf T}W_pq'|+p^{5/2}\bigr),$$ which is uniformly bounded. The normalized spherical integral of this expression on retained cells is $O(r_n)$. Indeed, $$q^{\mathsf T}W_pq-{q'}^{\mathsf T}W_pq'
 =\frac{2X^{\mathsf T}W_pX'
       -\rho(X^{\mathsf T}W_pX+{X'}^{\mathsf T}W_pX')}
        {n(1-\rho^2)}.$$ The diagonal terms cost $O(r_n)$. For the cross term, tilt a Gaussian pair at the cap saddle by $\pm cp^2X^{\mathsf T}W_pX'$, with $c$ small enough to preserve a fixed precision margin. The Gaussian logarithmic moment is $O_R(k_p)$, since $\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,\alpha}^2=O(n/p)$ and $\|R_{p,\alpha}h\|^2=O_R(np)$. The replica density bound <a href="#edge:replica-norm-density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:replica-norm-density">[edge:replica-norm-density]</a> costs a fixed factor. Hence $$\Pr_{\rm sp}\{|X^{\mathsf T}W_pX'|>t\}
       \le C e^{C_Rk_p-cp^2t}.$$ Integrating from a sufficiently large multiple of $np$ gives $\mathbb E_{\rm sp}|X^{\mathsf T}W_pX'|\le C_Rnp\le C_Rnr_n$. This full probability integral also bounds its unnormalized restriction to retained cells.

The bounded oscillation permits the mean value theorem for exponentials. After integration and summation over disjoint cells, the error is the preceding integrated $O(r_n)$; no supremum over frames is taken. Slightly enlarged boundary cells are paid by the pair tail. Thus $$E_UL_p(h)^2
 \le1+C_R\{nr_n^4+r_n+n^{-1}+e^{-cnr_n^3}\}.$$ Use $E_UL_p(h)=1$, $nr_n^4=n^{-1/3+4\cdot10^{-4}}$, and $nr_n^3=n^{3\cdot10^{-4}}$ to obtain <a href="#edge:likelihood-second-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:likelihood-second-moment">[edge:likelihood-second-moment]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-cube-caps"></a>
<div id="edge:cube-caps" class="lemma">

**Lemma 10** (Uniform cube cap estimates). *The static, curvature, and projection assertions <a href="#edge:static-estimates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:static-estimates">[edge:static-estimates]</a>–<a href="#edge:projection-tails" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:projection-tails">[edge:projection-tails]</a> hold on ordinary Gaussian disorder events of arbitrarily large limiting probability, with a tight threshold and every fixed field radius, tolerance, and scale buffer prescribed in Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>. The projection bound also holds for $P_qX/M_q$ under a cap interpolated linearly between $B_p$ and $B_q$, whenever $q\ge p$, $q/p$ is bounded, and the field lies in a fixed $q$-field ball.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-cube-caps"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-cube-caps</summary>

*Proof.* On dyadic $p$ and $v$, the spherical tail and <a href="#edge:bias-transfer" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:bias-transfer">[edge:bias-transfer]</a> give $$E_U[\mathbf 1_{\{L_\circ\ge1/2\}}
       \mu\{\|P_pX\|>vM_p\}]
       \le C e^{-c k_pv^6}.$$ Markov’s inequality with half the exponent has total failure at most $$\sum_{j,l\ge0}C e^{-cK\,8^j64^l}\le C e^{-c'K}.$$ The discarded $L_\circ<1/2$ event has probability $o(1)$ by <a href="#edge:haar-bias" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:haar-bias">[edge:haar-bias]</a>. Monotonicity of $P_p$, and a fixed-factor change in $M_p$, extend the uncapped result to every $p,v$.

The posterior tails follow deterministically. For $q\ge p$ of bounded ratio, let $B_\theta$ lie between $B_p$ and $B_q$. It is positive, supported on $\mathcal H_q$, and has norm at most $Cq^2$. Restricting the uncapped normalizer to $\|P_qX\|\le VM_q$ gives $$\mu e^{-X^{\mathsf T}B_\theta X/2}\ge e^{-Ck_q}$$ for a fixed large $V$. The zero-field capped law is even, so its normalizer for a linear field is at least one. On the shell $\|P_qX\|\asymp vM_q$, a field of norm at most $Rq^2M_q$ costs at most $Rk_qv$. This and the denominator cost are absorbed by the uncapped $e^{-c k_qv^6}$ tail for large $v$. This proves the posterior tail, including the interpolated assertion. The spherical argument is identical. The first two projection moments under all these posteriors are consequently bounded by $C_RM_q$ and $C_RM_q^2$.

<a id="edge:potential-interpolation"></a>
For nearby scales and fields, integrating first derivatives of the log partition function gives $$\label{edge:potential-interpolation}
 |\Delta\phi|\le C_Rk_q\left(
       |\Delta\log p|+\frac{\|\Delta h\|}{q^2M_q}\right),$$ and likewise for $\phi^{\rm sp}$. Indeed, $\|B_q-B_p\|\le Cq^2|\log(q/p)|$ on $\mathcal H_q$; its derivative is controlled by the second projection moment and the field derivative by the first. Fields in the smaller space are compared in $\mathcal H_q$.

<a id="edge:absolute-value-comparison"></a>
Cover $K\le k_p\le C_0\sqrt{\log n}$, with fixed $C_0$ large enough to overlap the source cutoff. Net scales from above and their spectral field balls at resolution $\eta/(C_R(1+C_0\sqrt{\log n}))$ in the units of <a href="#edge:potential-interpolation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:potential-interpolation">[edge:potential-interpolation]</a>. Conditional on the spectrum, these are deterministic nets. Since $\dim\mathcal H_p\le Ck_p$, their total size is $$\exp\{O_{\eta,R}(\sqrt{\log n}\log\log n)\}=n^{o(1)}.$$ At a net point <a href="#edge:likelihood-second-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:likelihood-second-moment">[edge:likelihood-second-moment]</a> and Chebyshev give $\Pr_U(|\log L_p(h)|>\eta/2)\le C_\eta n^{-1/4}$. The union bound and <a href="#edge:potential-interpolation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:potential-interpolation">[edge:potential-interpolation]</a> yield $$\label{edge:absolute-value-comparison}
 \sup_{\substack{K\le k_p\le C_0\sqrt{\log n}\\
                  \|h\|\le Rp^2M_p}}
 |\phi_p(h)-\phi_p^{\rm sp}(h)|\le\eta$$ with failure $n^{-1/4+o(1)}$, in addition to the projection event. For $k_p\ge c\sqrt{\log n}$, the cap and interpolation results of (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 2.6, Equation (2.11), and Lemma 2.7) <a id="pm-cite-38"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] apply as stated, since $C_1r_n$ is eventually below their fixed upper cutoff. Together these prove the value comparison at every scale.

For the mean, use this comparison on a larger ball. For unit $v\in\mathcal H_p$, freeze $\alpha=\alpha_p(h)$. The polar formula and Lemma <a href="#edge:norm-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:norm-density">5</a> give $$\log\mu_{p,h}^{\rm sp}
       e^{\pm t v^{\mathsf T}(X-R_{p,\alpha}h)}
       \le\tfrac12t^2v^{\mathsf T}R_{p,\alpha}v+C.$$ The cube bound has the additional $2\epsilon_vk_p$. Jensen with $t=\theta p^2M_p$, in the direction of the projected mean discrepancy, gives $$\frac{\|P_pm_p(h)-R_{p,\alpha}h\|}{M_p}
       \le C_R\theta+\frac{2\epsilon_v+C/k_p}{\theta}.$$ Choose $\theta$ from the required mean tolerance, then impose a smaller value tolerance and increase $K$.

It remains to prove the Hessian assertion on the low range. Put $\widehat R=R_{p,\alpha_p(h)}$, $m=\widehat Rh$, and $\sigma^2=2\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\widehat R^2+4m^{\mathsf T}\widehat Rm$. For a unit $v\in\mathcal H_p$ and $|\theta|\le1$, the shift $h+\theta pv$ fits a fixed larger ball because $p/(p^2M_p)=k_p^{-1/2}$. Freezing $\alpha$, the exact polar formula is $$\log\mu_{p,h}^{\rm sp} e^{\theta p v^{\mathsf T}(X-m)}
 =\tfrac12\theta^2p^2v^{\mathsf T}\widehat Rv+
       \log\frac{f_{\alpha,h+\theta pv}(n)}{f_{\alpha,h}(n)}.$$ The shifted mean $m_\theta=m+\theta p\widehat Rv$ satisfies $$\frac{\sigma_\theta^2}{\sigma^2}=1+O_R(k_p^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \frac{n-\mathbb E_\theta\|Y\|^2}{\sigma_\theta}
       =-\frac{2\theta p\langle m,\widehat Rv\rangle}{\sigma}
           +O_R(k_p^{-1/2}).$$ The leading term is uniformly bounded. The density estimate <a href="#edge:norm-local-limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:norm-local-limit">[edge:norm-local-limit]</a>, at this argument and at zero, gives <a id="edge:frozen-mgf-curvature"></a>$$\label{edge:frozen-mgf-curvature}
 \begin{split}
 \log\mu_{p,h}^{\rm sp} e^{\theta p v^{\mathsf T}(X-m)}
   &=\tfrac12\theta^2v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{p,h}v+O_R(k_p^{-1/2}),\\
 \Gamma_{p,h}
   &=p^2\left(\widehat R|_{\mathcal H_p}
       -\frac4{\sigma^2}(\widehat Rm)\otimes(\widehat Rm)\right).
 \end{split}$$ This is uniform in $h,v,\theta$. Cauchy–Schwarz and $\sigma^2\ge4m^{\mathsf T}\widehat Rm$ imply $0\preceq\Gamma_{p,h}\preceq C_RI$. Equation <a href="#edge:absolute-value-comparison" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:absolute-value-comparison">[edge:absolute-value-comparison]</a> changes the log moment by at most $2\eta$, so the cube error is at most $\delta=C_RK^{-1/2}+2\eta$.

<a id="edge:hessian-approximation"></a>
To justify differentiating this approximation, suppose a real $Z$ obeys $$\sup_{|\theta|\le1}
 \left|\log\mathbb Ee^{\theta Z}-a\theta^2/2\right|\le\delta,\qquad
 0\le a\le C,\quad 0<\delta\le1/16.$$ The values at $\pm1$ bound $\mathbb Ee^{|Z|}$, and hence bound the fourth derivative of $\psi(\theta)=\log\mathbb Ee^{\theta Z}$ on $[-1/2,1/2]$. Taylor’s formula gives $$\left|\psi''(0)
       -\frac{\psi(t)+\psi(-t)-2\psi(0)}{t^2}\right|\le C_Ct^2.$$ The assumed error changes this quotient by at most $2\delta/t^2$. With $t=\delta^{1/4}$, this proves $|\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}Z-a|\le C_C\sqrt\delta$. Applying it to $Z=pv^{\mathsf T}(X-m)$, for every unit $v$, yields $$\label{edge:hessian-approximation}
 \|p^2K_p(h)-\Gamma_{p,h}\|
       \le C_R\sqrt{C_RK^{-1/2}+2\eta}.$$

On the annulus put $t=\alpha/p^2$, $A=(n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\widehat R)/(np)$, $B=(p/n)\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\widehat R^2$, and $e=h/\|h\|$. Since $\widehat R|_{\mathcal H_p}=p^{-2}(1+t)^{-1}I$ and $m$ is parallel to $e$, $$\langle e,\Gamma_{p,h}e\rangle=\frac{B}{(1+t)B+2A}.$$ The trace estimates and denominator comparison give $A=b_0+O(\epsilon_{\rm sp}+s_0)$ and $B=2b_0+O(\epsilon_{\rm sp}+s_0)$, so this is $1/2+O(\epsilon_{\rm sp}+s_0)$. All other quadratic directions are bounded above by $(1-s_0)^{-1}$. Choose the spectral accuracy and $s_0$ small, then $\eta$ small and $K$ large in <a href="#edge:hessian-approximation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:hessian-approximation">[edge:hessian-approximation]</a>. This proves the annular curvature and radial deficit. On the entire ball, the saddle gap and the same estimate give $C_Rp^{-2}$, with $C_R$ fixed before the annular tolerance. The source curvature assertion covers the higher range. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-15"></a>
#### Location and covariance of the observation path

The uniform cap event controls external fields. We now locate the random field produced by the Gibbs observation. A shrinking annulus will give an averaged covariance estimate; a fixed annulus gives the stronger exponential tail needed in Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>.

<a id="edge:conditioned-spectral-event"></a>
We first state the additional eigenvalue-only restriction used for norm conditioning. Put $$b_n=1+(-g_{1,n})_+,\qquad
 \ell_{a,n}=(g_{a,n}+b_n)^{-1},\qquad
 D_n=n^{1/3}-\sum_a\ell_{a,n},$$ and let $q_n$ be the density of $\sum_a\ell_{a,n}(\xi_a^2-1)$ for independent standard normal $\xi_a$. For every $\chi>0$, one may fix sufficiently large integers $m,J_\chi$ and positive constants $c_\chi,C_\chi$ so that an eigenvalue-only event $\mathcal S_n^{\rm ann}(\chi)$ satisfies $\liminf_n\mathbb P(\mathcal S_n^{\rm ann}(\chi))\ge1-\chi$ and, on it, $$\label{edge:conditioned-spectral-event}
 \begin{gathered}
 b_n\le C_\chi,\qquad \ell_{a,n}\ge c_\chi\quad(1\le a\le m),\\
 g_{a,n}\ge C_\chi^{-1}a^{2/3}\quad(J_\chi<a\le n),\qquad
 q_n(D_n)\ge c_\chi.
 \end{gathered}$$ These restrictions follow from the eigenvalue bounds in (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 2.1) <a id="pm-cite-39"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)], finite edge-coordinate convergence, and the density argument in its Proposition 2.3. We intersect this event with the local spectral event of Lemma <a href="#edge:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spectral">4</a> and $\mathcal S_n^{\rm glob}$, assigning a portion of the prescribed failure probability to it. The eigenvalue events of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 2.5) <a id="pm-cite-40"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] needed for <a href="#edge:haar-bias" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:haar-bias">[edge:haar-bias]</a> are retained separately. All constants below may depend on the prescribed confidence; no fixed density lower bound on an event of probability $1-o(1)$ is asserted.

<a id="stmt-edge-path-annuli"></a>
<div id="edge:path-annuli" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:shrinking-annulus"></a>
<a id="edge:fixed-annulus-biased"></a>
**Lemma 11** (The observation annuli). *On the fixed spectral restrictions, there are $a_{\rm an},c,C>0$ such that for every dyadic interval $[q,2q]$ with fixed buffers inside the enlarged scale range, $$\label{edge:shrinking-annulus}
 \mathbf P\left\{\exists p\in[q,2q]:
       |\alpha_p(h_p)|>Ck_p^{-1/10}p^2\right\}
       \le C e^{-c k_q^{a_{\rm an}}}.$$ For every fixed $\zeta>0$, after increasing the threshold, $$\label{edge:fixed-annulus-biased}
 \mathbf P\left\{\exists p\in[q,2q]:
       |\alpha_p(h_p)|>\zeta p^2\right\}
       \le C_\zeta e^{-c_\zeta k_q}.$$ Consequently <a href="#edge:ordinary-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:ordinary-annulus">[edge:ordinary-annulus]</a> holds simultaneously at every scale on ordinary disorder events of arbitrarily large limiting probability.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-path-annuli"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-path-annuli</summary>

<a id="edge:leading-resolvent-sum"></a>
*Proof.* By <a href="#edge:haar-bias" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:haar-bias">[edge:haar-bias]</a>, under $\mathbf P$ the spectral spin is spherical. Its Gaussian representation is that of (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 2.3) <a id="pm-cite-41"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. The annulus calculation in (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 3.1, Equation (3.1)) <a id="pm-cite-42"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] is stated for the source observation range beginning at $r_n$; the tight-threshold dyadic estimates below extend that calculation to the scales used here. Set $D_i'=d_i+b_nn^{-2/3}=n^{-2/3}(g_{i,n}+b_n)$. Before conditioning, let $Y_i$ be independent $N(0,(D_i')^{-1})$; conditioning on $\sum_iY_i^2=n$ gives the spherical law. The definition of $b_n$ gives $\min_iD_i'\ge n^{-2/3}$, while <a href="#edge:conditioned-spectral-event" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:conditioned-spectral-event">[edge:conditioned-spectral-event]</a> supplies the fixed leading variance lower bounds. The density of $n^{-2/3}\sum_iY_i^2$ at $n^{1/3}$ is exactly $q_n(D_n)$, and hence is bounded below on the chosen spectral set. The same set and the active count give $$\label{edge:leading-resolvent-sum}
 \sum_{d_i\le p^2}(D_i')^{-1}
   =n^{2/3}\sum_{d_i\le p^2}\ell_{i,n}
   \le Cn^{2/3}(1+k_p^{1/3})\le Cnp.$$ Indeed the first $J_\chi$ terms are bounded by one, and the remaining terms are bounded by $C_\chi i^{-2/3}$.

Let $\vartheta=p^2+b_nn^{-2/3}$ and, before conditioning, write $h_{p,i}=B_{p,i}Y_i+B_{p,i}^{1/2}Z_i$. The quadratic form obtained from $\|h_p\|^2-\vartheta^2\|Y\|^2$ has mean $-\vartheta^2\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,b_nn^{-2/3}}$. On an active coordinate the coefficient of the standardized $Y_i^2$ term is $$\frac{B_{p,i}^2-\vartheta^2}{D_i'}=D_i'-2\vartheta=O(p^2);$$ the cross coefficient is $O(p^3/\sqrt{D_i'})$. Equation <a href="#edge:leading-resolvent-sum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:leading-resolvent-sum">[edge:leading-resolvent-sum]</a> and the capped second trace bound therefore show that the matrix of this quadratic form, in the standardized $(Y,Z)$ variables, satisfies $$\|\mathsf A_p\|_{\rm F}^2\le Cp^4k_p,\qquad
 \|\mathsf A_p\|\le Cp^2k_p^{1/3}.$$ The Gaussian quadratic-form moment formula for its centered version bounds a deviation of $p^2k_p^{9/10}$ by $$C\exp\left[-c\min\{k_p^{4/5},k_p^{17/30}\}\right].$$ This remains true after norm conditioning, with a constant loss. Indeed use the same exponential tilt, with parameter at most one eighth of $\|\mathsf A_p\|^{-1}$. Its joint covariance and its $Y$-marginal covariance stay comparable to the originals. A fixed number of the leading marginal variances bounds the density of $n^{-2/3}\|Y\|^2$ from above by a constant, through the characteristic formula <a href="#edge:norm-characteristic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:norm-characteristic">[edge:norm-characteristic]</a>. The original density at $n^{1/3}$ is bounded below on the chosen spectral set. The polar density ratio therefore costs a constant.

After conditioning, the deterministic target for $\|h_p\|^2$ is $\ell_p(b_nn^{-2/3})^2\asymp p^2k_p$. The preceding error is a relative $O(k_p^{-1/10})$. It first places the inferred saddle in a fixed annulus. On that annulus $\mathrm d(\ell_p(u)^2)/\mathrm du\asymp k_p$. Hence $$|\alpha_p(h_p)-b_nn^{-2/3}|\le Cp^2k_p^{-1/10}.$$ Since $b_nn^{-2/3}/p^2=O(k_p^{-2/3})$, this proves the fixed-scale version of <a href="#edge:shrinking-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:shrinking-annulus">[edge:shrinking-annulus]</a>.

For a whole interval use a mesh of spacing $k_q^{-3}$ in $\log p$. Its size is polynomial in $k_q$. Except with $Ce^{-ck_q}$ probability, the spherical projection at the upper endpoint is at most $CM_q$, by Lemma <a href="#edge:spherical-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spherical-tails">6</a>. The signal increments on a mesh gap are then at most $Cq^2M_qk_q^{-3}$. The noise increments have covariance norm $O(q^2k_q^{-3})$. A constant-resolution net of the sphere in $O(k_q)$ dimensions and the Gaussian maximal inequality show that their norm on every gap is less than $q^2M_qk_q^{-1/10}$, except with $Ce^{-ck_q}$ probability. The target length is Lipschitz in the same scaled units: between activations differentiate the capped trace, using the active count and second trace; the target is continuous at activations. These observations interpolate the fixed-scale bound. The polynomial mesh size is absorbed by decreasing the positive exponent, proving <a href="#edge:shrinking-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:shrinking-annulus">[edge:shrinking-annulus]</a>.

For a fixed $\zeta$, it suffices by inclusion to treat $\zeta$ below a fixed small annulus width. The stronger exponent follows from a different Gaussian reference, following the source-range fixed saddle test in (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 19.2, Equation (19.9) and its proof) <a id="pm-cite-43"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)]. Fix a small $\xi>0$, to be chosen after $\zeta$, and let $$R_\xi=(2+\xi p^2-W)^{-1},\qquad
 Y\sim N(0,R_\xi),\qquad h_p=B_pY+\beta_p .$$ Increase $K$ so that $d_1\ge-\xi p^2/2$. The vector $a_{p,\xi}=R_{p,\xi p^2}h_p$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $$C_{p,\xi}=R_\xi-R_{p,\xi p^2}.$$ The resolvent and clipped traces give $$\left|\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}C_{p,\xi}-(n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_{p,0})\right|
       \le C\sqrt\xi\,np+o_K(np),\qquad
 \|C_{p,\xi}\|\le C(\xi p^2)^{-1},\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}C_{p,\xi}^2\le Cn/(\sqrt\xi\,p).$$ For a fixed multiple of $np$, exponential Markov with both signs of a sufficiently small multiple of $\xi p^2$ therefore gives a deviation cost $e^{-c_\zeta\xi k_p}$, once $\xi$ is sufficiently small. The centered logarithmic moment costs $O(\xi^{3/2}k_p)$, whereas the Markov gain is a fixed multiple of $\zeta\xi k_p$.

We spell out the norm-conditioning cost. The deficit $n-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}R_\xi$ is between fixed multiples of $\sqrt\xi\,np$, after increasing $K$ for this fixed $\xi$. A leading variance is comparable to $(\xi p^2)^{-1}$; the other squared norms have variance at most $Cn/(\sqrt\xi\,p)$. Chebyshev places the residual length in a fixed interval comparable to $\sqrt\xi\,np$ when $K\gg\xi^{-3/2}$. On this interval the leading Gaussian-square density is at least $$C_\xi^{-1}\sqrt{p/n}\exp(-C\xi^{3/2}k_p).$$ This is a lower bound for the original norm density by convolution. Under the quadratic tilt used above, the marginal covariance of $Y$ retains $ck_p$ independent spectral rows with covariance comparable to $p^{-2}$; the tilt keeps the joint covariance comparable. Equation <a href="#edge:replica-norm-density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:replica-norm-density">[edge:replica-norm-density]</a> bounds its norm density by $C_\xi\sqrt{p/n}$. Thus conditioning costs at most $C_\xi e^{C\xi^{3/2}k_p}$.

Since $R_{p,0}h_p=(1+\xi)R_{p,\xi p^2}h_p$, compare the saddle length at the two boundaries $\alpha=\pm\zeta p^2$. The derivative bounds in <a href="#edge:scaled-saddle" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:scaled-saddle">[edge:scaled-saddle]</a>, and monotonicity beyond those boundaries, put $\{|\alpha_p(h_p)|>\zeta p^2\}$ inside the relaxed squared-length deviation just bounded. Choose $\xi$ so that its $O(\sqrt\xi)$ target error fits the $\zeta$ tolerance and $C\xi^{3/2}<c_\zeta\xi/2$. The conditioned deviation then has probability $C_\zeta e^{-c_\zeta'k_p}$. The same $k_q^{-3}$ mesh proves <a href="#edge:fixed-annulus-biased" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:fixed-annulus-biased">[edge:fixed-annulus-biased]</a>.

Finally take $q_j=2^j(K/n)^{1/3}$. By <a href="#edge:bias-transfer" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:bias-transfer">[edge:bias-transfer]</a> and Markov, the ordinary whole-interval probability is at most $Ce^{-c k_{q_j}}$ outside disorder probability $Ce^{-c k_{q_j}}$, after decreasing $c$. Their sum is $$\sum_{j\ge0}Ce^{-cK8^j}\le Ce^{-c'K}.$$ Use <a href="#edge:haar-bias" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:haar-bias">[edge:haar-bias]</a> for $L_\circ<1/2$ and increase $K$. Every scale lies in one such interval and $k_p\asymp k_{q_j}$ there, proving <a href="#edge:ordinary-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:ordinary-annulus">[edge:ordinary-annulus]</a> simultaneously in $p$. ◻

</details>

We now fix the finite set of auxiliary radii, buffers, and tolerances used in the covariance argument. Fix once a sufficiently small $\gamma>0$, as specified by the compression argument below. Then choose finite $C_*$ so that the range through $C_*r_n$ contains all parent intervals $[q/(2\gamma),q/\gamma]$, $q\le r_n$, and their prescribed enlargements, as well as the range through $C_1r_n$. Choose $\eta$ sufficiently small compared with $\gamma^2$, and an auxiliary curvature tolerance $\epsilon_{\rm aux}$ sufficiently small compared with $\eta$; it may be smaller than the prescribed $\epsilon_0$. The extension construction below prescribes an auxiliary width $s_{\rm aux}$, static tolerances, radii, and a threshold for these choices. They are further cap requests under the finite-intersection convention after Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>. Let $\mathcal G_n^{\rm aux}$ be the event, measurable from $W$, on which Lemma <a href="#edge:cube-caps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:cube-caps">10</a> holds with these choices. Let $\mathcal G_n^{\rm FUA}$ be the entire good-disorder event $\mathcal G_n$ defined in (OpenAI 2026d, sec. 3) <a id="pm-cite-44"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] for its Proposition 4.2, with that source’s fixed tolerances and full scale and field ranges. This event has ordinary Gaussian-disorder probability tending to one. Set $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_n^{\rm aux}\cap\mathcal G_n^{\rm FUA}$. Below we use the source covariance conclusion on the terminal interval $[r_n,C_\gamma r_n]$, which is contained in its stated interval $[r_n,p_*]$ for all sufficiently large $n$. All probabilities below are measured under $\mathbf P$ before restriction to $\mathcal G$. On each chosen spectral set, the constants are uniform.

<a id="stmt-edge-score-covariance"></a>
<div id="edge:score-covariance" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:score-bound"></a>
<a id="edge:frobenius-bound"></a>
**Lemma 12** (Integrated score and covariance error). *Let $I=[q,2q]$, with a prescribed fixed multiplicative enlargement inside the scale range. At path fields write $$a_p=P_p(m_p-m_p^{\rm sp}),\qquad D_p=p^2K_p-I_{\mathcal H_p}.$$ There are $c,C,a_1>0$ such that $$\label{edge:score-bound}
 \mathbf P\left\{
   \int_I\|a_p\|^2\,\mathrm d(p^2)>Ck_q^{1/2}\right\}
       \le C e^{-c k_q^{a_1}},$$ and $$\label{edge:frobenius-bound}
 \mathbf P\left(
 \mathcal G\cap
 \left\{\int_q^{2q}\frac{\|D_p\|_{\rm F}^2}{k_p}\,\mathrm d\log p
              >Ck_q^{-1/5}\right\}\right)
       \le C e^{-c k_q^{a_1}} .$$ The same statements hold for every fixed enlargement of $I$, with adjusted constants. They are probability statements; no expectation of the untruncated score on their failures is asserted.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-score-covariance"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-score-covariance</summary>

*Proof.* Put $t=p^2$, and include $U$ in the observation filtration, so that every disorder event is measurable at time zero. The exact likelihood identity <a href="#edge:path-likelihood" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:path-likelihood">[edge:path-likelihood]</a> yields <a id="edge:likelihood-sde"></a>$$\label{edge:likelihood-sde}
 \mathrm d\log L_{\sqrt t}
       =a_{\sqrt t}\cdot\mathrm d\mathcal B_t
          +\tfrac12\|a_{\sqrt t}\|^2\,\mathrm dt,$$ where $\mathcal B$ is the continuous cube innovation martingale with $\mathrm d\langle\mathcal B\rangle_t=P_{\sqrt t}\,\mathrm dt$; the coefficients lie in the active space. This is the exact filtering calculation in (OpenAI 2026d, proof of Lemma 3.5, after Equation (3.7)) <a id="pm-cite-45"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]; it follows as well by differentiating the posterior partition function, including the interaction change $-\mathrm dB_{\sqrt t}$. There is no jump in $\log L$ at activation.

At a deterministic endpoint and for $H>0$, <a href="#edge:path-likelihood" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:path-likelihood">[edge:path-likelihood]</a> gives $$\mathbf P(\log L_p<-H)\le e^{-H}.$$ For a fixed $R_0$ containing the path annulus, put $\mathcal U_p=\{\widetilde h:\|\widetilde h\|\le R_0p^2M_p\}$. Lemma <a href="#edge:replica-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:replica-comparison">9</a> gives $$\mathbf P(\log L_p>H,h_p\in\mathcal U_p)
 \le e^{-H}\int_{\mathcal U_p}Q^{\rm sp}(\mathrm d\widetilde h)\,
          E_U L_p(\widetilde h)^2
 \le (1+Cn^{-1/4})e^{-H}.$$ The field in the inner expectation is deterministic. Lemma <a href="#edge:path-annuli" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:path-annuli">11</a> excludes the complementary endpoint fields with probability $Ce^{-c k_q^{a_{\rm an}}}$.

On an enlarged interval write $\mathcal J_I=\int\|a_p\|^2\,\mathrm d(p^2)$ and $M=\int a_p\cdot\mathrm d\mathcal B_{p^2}$. On the two endpoint events just given, $M+\mathcal J_I/2\le2H$. If $\mathcal J_I\ge8H$, then $M\le-\mathcal J_I/4$. The positive exponential supermartingale $\exp(-M/4-\mathcal J_I/32)$ bounds this event by $e^{-H/4}$. Taking $H=Ck_q^{1/2}$ proves <a href="#edge:score-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:score-bound">[edge:score-bound]</a>.

<a id="edge:score-energy"></a>
Between activations the two filtering equations give, with $\Delta_t=K_{\sqrt t}-K_{\sqrt t}^{\rm sp}$, $$\mathrm da_{\sqrt t}
       =\Delta_t\,\mathrm d\mathcal B_t
          -K_{\sqrt t}^{\rm sp}a_{\sqrt t}\,\mathrm dt .$$ Choose a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\chi(t)$, equal to one on the target interval, zero at the ends of a fixed enlargement, and with $|t\chi'(t)|\le C$. The integrated Itô identity is $$\label{edge:score-energy}
 \begin{split}
 \int\chi t\|\Delta_t\|_{\rm F}^2\,\mathrm dt
 ={}&-\int(\chi+t\chi')\|a_{\sqrt t}\|^2\,\mathrm dt
       +2\int\chi t\langle a_{\sqrt t},
                         K_{\sqrt t}^{\rm sp}a_{\sqrt t}\rangle\,\mathrm dt\\
 &-\mathcal M
   -\sum_j\chi(t_j)t_j
       \|\Delta P_j(m_{\sqrt{t_j}}-m_{\sqrt{t_j}}^{\rm sp})\|^2,\\
 \mathcal M={}&2\int\chi t
       \langle a_{\sqrt t},\Delta_t\,\mathrm d\mathcal B_t\rangle .
 \end{split}$$ Here $\Delta P_j$ is the jump of $P_{\sqrt t}$ at the activation time $t_j$. The sum has the favorable sign. On $\mathcal G$ and the whole-path annulus event, the coarse bounds give $\|tK_{\sqrt t}\|+\|tK_{\sqrt t}^{\rm sp}\|\le C$. Thus the left side on the target interval is bounded by $C\mathcal J_I+C|\mathcal M|$.

For concentration, stop only the stochastic integral at the first annulus failure, and set its integrand to zero on $\mathcal G^c$. The latter event is measurable at time zero. The stopped bracket is at most $C\mathcal J_I$, and the stopped integral agrees with $\mathcal M$ on $\mathcal G$ and the whole-path annulus event. The exponential bracket inequality, <a href="#edge:score-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:score-bound">[edge:score-bound]</a>, and <a href="#edge:shrinking-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:shrinking-annulus">[edge:shrinking-annulus]</a> consequently bound the target integral of $\|p^2(K_p-K_p^{\rm sp})\|_{\rm F}^2\,\mathrm d\log p$ by $Ck_q^{1/2}$, with the required exceptional probability intersected with $\mathcal G$. The full identity <a href="#edge:score-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:score-energy">[edge:score-energy]</a> was not stopped, so it has no terminal boundary term.

On the shrinking annulus, rotational invariance inside the flat cap gives one spherical transverse covariance eigenvalue $\kappa_\perp$ and one radial eigenvalue. The frozen linear moment bound at shifts $\pm pe$ gives $$|e^{\mathsf T}(m_p^{\rm sp}-R_{p,\alpha}h_p)|\le C/p.$$ Since $\kappa_\perp=(e^{\mathsf T}m_p^{\rm sp})/\|h_p\|$ and $\|h_p\|\asymp p^2M_p$, $$|p^2\kappa_\perp-1|
       \le C(k_p^{-1/10}+k_p^{-1/2}).$$ The scaled radial covariance is bounded by the spherical version of <a href="#edge:hessian-approximation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:hessian-approximation">[edge:hessian-approximation]</a>. There are $O(k_p)$ transverse dimensions and one radial dimension, so $$\frac{\|p^2K_p^{\rm sp}-I\|_{\rm F}^2}{k_p}
       \le C(k_p^{-1/5}+k_p^{-1}).$$ Combine this with the preceding cube–sphere covariance estimate, divide by $k_q\asymp k_p$, and decrease $a_1>0$ if necessary. This proves <a href="#edge:frobenius-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:frobenius-bound">[edge:frobenius-bound]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-16"></a>
#### The covariance iteration and exact-scale variance

The Frobenius estimate says that most directions have a small covariance error on average over a scale interval. To control the largest positive error, compare a child cap to a larger parent cap. The radial deficit puts every positive error in the tangent space of the parent field; the unused Haar rotation then dilutes it in the smaller child space.

<a id="edge:transition-covariance"></a>
Use the fixed small $\gamma>0$ above. Let $q$ be a child scale and $p$ a parent scale with $x=q/p\in[\gamma,2\gamma]$, and put $\Delta=B_p-B_q$. Conditional on $W$ and observations through $q$, $h_p$ has law <a id="edge:transition"></a>$$\label{edge:transition}
 \mathsf T_{q,p,h_q}(\mathrm dy)
 =\frac{e^{\phi_p(y)}N(h_q,\Delta)(\mathrm dy)}
        {\int e^{\phi_p(z)}N(h_q,\Delta)(\mathrm dz)} .$$ The Gaussian is on the positive-increment space. Its covariance compressed to $\mathcal H_q$ is $\Delta_q=(1-x^2)p^2I_{\mathcal H_q}$. Differentiation of the convolution gives the exact identity from (OpenAI 2026d, sec. 4.1, Equation (4.3)) <a id="pm-cite-46"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)], $$\label{edge:transition-covariance}
 K_q=\Delta_q^{-1}
       [\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}_{\mathsf T_{q,p,h_q}}(h_p)]_{\mathcal H_q}\Delta_q^{-1}
       -\Delta_q^{-1}.$$

<a id="stmt-edge-annular-extension"></a>
<div id="edge:annular-extension" class="lemma">

**Lemma 13** (An extension on the parent annulus). *Choose $\eta>0$ sufficiently small compared with $\gamma^2$, then the coarse curvature tolerance $\epsilon_{\rm aux}$ sufficiently small compared with $\eta$. One can choose $s_{\rm aux}$, the static tolerances, and the threshold $K$ so that the following holds on $\mathcal G$. For every child field satisfying $|\alpha_q(h_q)|\le s_{\rm aux}q^2$, put $$\mathcal A_p=\{h:|\alpha_p(h)|\le s_{\rm aux}p^2/2\},\qquad
 \mathcal A_p^+=\{h:|\alpha_p(h)|<3s_{\rm aux}p^2/4\}.$$ There is a semiconcave extension $\bar\phi_p$ with upper Hessian bound $(1+\eta)p^{-2}I$, agreeing with $\phi_p$ on $\mathcal A_p^+$. Moreover, $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal A_p,(\mathcal A_p^+)^c)\ge c_{\rm buf}p^2M_p$ for a fixed $c_{\rm buf}>0$. Under both $\mathsf T_{q,p,h_q}$ and the transition obtained by replacing $\phi_p$ with $\bar\phi_p$, the probability of $\mathcal A_p^c$ is at most $Ce^{-c_1k_p}$. The same bound holds with any fixed polynomial moment of $\|h_p\|/(p^2M_p)$ inserted, after decreasing $c_1>0$. All constants are uniform in the indicated fields and scales.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-annular-extension"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-annular-extension</summary>

*Proof.* We verify the deterministic extension proof of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 4.3) <a id="pm-cite-47"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)], following (OpenAI 2026b, Proposition 16.1) <a id="pm-cite-48"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)], with the new lower threshold. On $\{|\alpha_p|\le3s_{\rm aux}p^2/4\}$ take the infimum, over $z$, of $$\phi_p(z)+\nabla\phi_p(z)\cdot(y-z)
       +\frac{1+\eta}{2p^2}\|y-z\|^2.$$ Choose $s_{\rm aux}\ll\eta,\gamma^2$. The length bounds in Lemma <a href="#edge:norm-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:norm-density">5</a> give a fixed $\beta_{\rm buf}>0$ such that a segment of length at most $\beta_{\rm buf}p^2M_p$ starting in this smaller annulus remains in the full annulus. For such pairs the supporting inequality follows by integrating the coarse Hessian bound. For $\|y-z\|\ge\beta_{\rm buf}p^2M_p$, freeze the spherical saddle at $z$. The polar linear-moment bound gives the spherical quadratic support with Hessian $(p^2+\alpha_p(z))^{-1}I$, its saddle gradient, and a bounded norm-density error. The static value and mean estimates add $2\epsilon_vk_p+\epsilon_gM_p\|y-z\|$. Relative to $\|y-z\|^2/(2p^2)$, the total residual is bounded by $$Cs_{\rm aux}+\frac{4\epsilon_v+C/k_p}{\beta_{\rm buf}^2}
       +\frac{2\epsilon_g}{\beta_{\rm buf}} .$$ Choose $s_{\rm aux}$, then $\beta_{\rm buf}$, then $\epsilon_v,\epsilon_g$ so that this is less than $\eta$, and finally increase $K$. Every support lies above $\phi_p$ on the smaller annulus. Its infimum is finite and semiconcave with the stated upper Hessian, and it agrees there by choosing $z=y$. The length derivative gives $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal A_p,(\mathcal A_p^+)^c)\ge c_{\rm buf}p^2M_p$.

For the transition tails freeze the child saddle $\alpha=\alpha_q(h_q)$, and use as reference the Gaussian transition tilted by the parent frozen quadratic $q_{W_p,\alpha}$. Writing $R_u=R_{u,\alpha}$, Gaussian convolution gives <a id="edge:reference-transition"></a>$$\label{edge:reference-transition}
 R_ph_p\sim N(R_qh_q,R_q-R_p),\qquad R_q^{-1}=R_p^{-1}-\Delta.$$ The child saddle equation shows that $\mathbb E\|h_p\|^2=\ell_p(\alpha)^2$, exactly. The field covariance has norm at most $C\gamma^{-2}p^2$. Gaussian concentration of its norm therefore gives $$\Pr_{\rm ref}\{|\|h_p\|-\ell_p(\alpha)|>vp^2M_p\}
       \le C e^{-c\gamma^2k_pv^2},
 \qquad v\ge C/(\gamma\sqrt{k_p}).$$ The reference radius lies strictly inside $\mathcal A_p$: $|\alpha|\le s_{\rm aux}q^2\le4s_{\rm aux}\gamma^2p^2$. The length derivative gives a fixed positive gap in units $p^2M_p$ to the boundary of $\mathcal A_p$.

Choose $z_0\in\mathcal H_p$ with $\|z_0\|=\ell_p(\alpha)$ and calibrate the reference quadratic by $$q^\sharp(y)=q_{W_p,\alpha}(y)+\log f_{W_p,\alpha,z_0}(n).$$ The active covariance is scalar, so the added density depends only on $\|z_0\|$; the additive constant leaves the reference transition unchanged. On bounded scaled radii, the noncentral upper norm-density bound and the static value comparison give $\phi_p(y)-q^\sharp(y)\le\epsilon k_p+O(1)$, with any prescribed fixed $\epsilon>0$. Outside a sufficiently large bounded radius, the zero-field projection tail gives $$\phi_p(y)-\phi_p(0)
 \le Ck_p\left(1+
       \left(\frac{\|y\|}{p^2M_p}\right)^{6/5}\right).$$ This follows by maximizing the exponent $uv-cv^6$ after integrating the tail against a linear field of scaled length $u$. Its growth is strictly subquadratic. For the extension choose the support centered at the point of radius $\ell_p(\alpha)$ in the direction of $y$. At distance $vp^2M_p$, its excess over the reference is at most $$\epsilon k_p(1+v)+C(\eta+s_{\rm aux})k_pv^2+O(1).$$ This uses the static mean error for the linear term and the difference of the two quadratic coefficients for the last term. Choose $\eta+s_{\rm aux}\ll\gamma^2$, and then $\epsilon$ small compared with the squared fixed gap to $\mathcal A_p^c$. Outside $\mathcal A_p$ these errors are smaller than the reference Gaussian deviation cost.

The normalizing integrals relative to the reference are at least $e^{-\epsilon'k_p}$ for any needed fixed $\epsilon'>0$. To see this, integrate over a thin fixed shell about the reference radius, contained in $\mathcal A_p$. Its reference probability is bounded below when $K$ is large. On that shell the frozen density formula <a href="#edge:frozen-density" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:frozen-density">[edge:frozen-density]</a> bounds the off-saddle logarithmic density loss by $C\tau^2k_p+O(1)$ when the shell width is $\tau$ in scaled units: the first parameter derivative vanishes at the saddle and the second is one quarter of the norm-square variance $O(n/p)$. The static lower value error adds only $\epsilon_vk_p$. Take $\tau$ and $\epsilon_v$ sufficiently small. Both potentials agree on this shell. Dividing the preceding upper tail integrals by this lower bound proves the stated disagreement tails. Polynomial moments are absorbed by the same quadratic reference tail and the subquadratic bound at large radii. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-edge-positive-curvature"></a>
<div id="edge:positive-curvature" class="lemma">

<a id="edge:positive-curvature-bound"></a>
**Lemma 14** (Positive covariance error). *For some $a,c,C>0$, uniformly at every deterministic scale $K\le k_p$, $p\le r_n$, apart from activation points, $$\label{edge:positive-curvature-bound}
 \mathbf P\left(
 \mathcal G\cap
 \{p^2K_p\npreceq(1+Ck_p^{-a})I_{\mathcal H_p}\}\right)
       \le C e^{-c k_p^a}.$$ The probability is taken before restricting to $\mathcal G$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-positive-curvature"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-positive-curvature</summary>

<a id="edge:local-parent-validity"></a>
*Proof.* Fix a deterministic nonactivation scale $p$ on the retained spectral set. For $h\in\mathcal H_p$, write $D_p(h)=p^2K_p(h)-I_{\mathcal H_p}$. Define a Borel predicate $\mathcal V_p(W_p,h)$ to be false unless $h\in\mathcal H_p$, the saddle $\alpha_p(h)$ exists, and $h\ne0$. Otherwise, with $e=h/\|h\|$, it requires $$\label{edge:local-parent-validity}
 |\alpha_p(h)|\le s_{\rm aux}p^2,\qquad
 p^2K_p(h)\preceq(1+\epsilon_{\rm aux})I_{\mathcal H_p},\qquad
 p^2\langle e,K_p(h)e\rangle\le0.9.$$ This condition contains no restriction to $\mathcal G$. At a nonactivation scale, $P_p$ is the spectral projection of $W_p$ at its flat eigenvalue $2-p^2$, and $R_{p,u}=(2I-W_p+uI)^{-1}$. Thus the predicate, the saddle, and the covariance used here are determined by $(p,W_p,h)$. Their defining formulas are jointly Borel away from activation scales. In the rest of the proof these objects are evaluated at $h=h_p$, and that argument is suppressed.

<a id="edge:tangent-bounds"></a>
On $\mathcal V_p$, use blocks relative to $\mathcal H_p=\operatorname{span}\{e\}\oplus(\mathcal H_p\cap e^\perp)$, put $z=(D_p)_{\perp e}$, and define on $\mathcal H_p\cap e^\perp$ <a id="edge:tangent-error"></a>$$\label{edge:tangent-error}
 E_p=\left((D_p)_{\perp\perp}
             +\frac{zz^{\mathsf T}}{|(D_p)_{ee}|}\right)_+,
 \qquad \widehat s_p=\|(D_p)_+\|.$$ Extend $E_p$ by zero on the radial direction and on $\mathcal H_p^\perp$. Off $\mathcal V_p$, set both $E_p$ and $\widehat s_p$ to zero, before any restriction to $\mathcal G$. Covariance positivity and <a href="#edge:local-parent-validity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:local-parent-validity">[edge:local-parent-validity]</a> give $-I\preceq D_p\preceq\epsilon_{\rm aux}I$ and $(D_p)_{ee}\le-0.1$ on $\mathcal V_p$. Maximizing the quadratic form of $D_p$ over its radial coordinate, and then taking the positive part on $e^\perp$, gives $$\label{edge:tangent-bounds}
 D_p\preceq E_p,\qquad
 \|E_p\|\le C\widehat s_p,\qquad
 \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}E_p}{k_p}
       \le C\frac{\|D_p\|_{\rm F}}{\sqrt{k_p}}+\frac C{k_p}$$ on $\mathcal V_p$, with $D_p\preceq E_p$ understood on $\mathcal H_p$. For the norm bound, the maximizing radial coordinate of a unit transverse vector is bounded because the radial deficit is fixed and $D_p$ is bounded; compare the resulting vector with $D_p\preceq\widehat s_pI$. For the trace, the rank-one correction has bounded trace, and $\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}(((D_p)_{\perp\perp})_+)\le
\sqrt{\dim\mathcal H_p}\|D_p\|_{\rm F}$; the displayed trace bound also uses $\dim\mathcal H_p\le Ck_p$ from the retained spectral set. These are the algebraic bounds of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 4.4, Equation (4.4)) <a id="pm-cite-49"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]. In particular $\widehat s_p\le\epsilon_{\rm aux}$ and $\|E_p\|\le C\epsilon_{\rm aux}$ everywhere, including on disorder failures. Include $C\epsilon_{\rm aux}\ll\gamma^2$ in the initial auxiliary choice.

Apply Brascamp–Lieb’s covariance inequality (Brascamp and Lieb 1976) <a id="pm-cite-50"></a>[[BrascampLieb1976](#ref-BrascampLieb1976)] to the transition with $\bar\phi_p$. After whitening, its Hessian has a fixed positive margin because $\Delta\preceq(1-x^2)p^2I$ and $\eta\ll\gamma^2$. If $\bar K$ is the extended Hessian, the covariance is at most the transition expectation of $$\Delta^{1/2}
 (I-\Delta^{1/2}\bar K\Delta^{1/2})^{-1}\Delta^{1/2}.$$ Mollify the semiconcave extension to apply the smooth inequality and pass to the limit using the positive margin. Lemma <a href="#edge:annular-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:annular-extension">13</a> replaces the extended Hessian and transition by $K_p$ and the true transition on agreement. Its polynomially weighted tails control first and second moments on the complement. In field units the covariance error is $O(p^4M_p^2e^{-c k_p})$; after <a href="#edge:transition-covariance" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:transition-covariance">[edge:transition-covariance]</a> and multiplication by $q^2$, the remaining polynomial factor in $k_p$ is absorbed by decreasing the exponent.

<a id="edge:parent-inequality"></a>
On $\mathcal G$, the agreement annulus lies in $\mathcal V_p$, so <a href="#edge:tangent-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:tangent-bounds">[edge:tangent-bounds]</a> gives $K_p\preceq p^{-2}(I+E_p)$. Put $A=I-\Delta/p^2$ and $S=p^{-2}\Delta^{1/2}E_p\Delta^{1/2}$. Then $A\succeq x^2I$ and $\|A^{-1/2}SA^{-1/2}\|\ll1$, so $$(A-S)^{-1}\preceq A^{-1}+2A^{-1}SA^{-1}.$$ The baseline $A^{-1}$, substituted in <a href="#edge:transition-covariance" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:transition-covariance">[edge:transition-covariance]</a>, is exactly $q^{-2}I_{\mathcal H_q}$. For the correction, the two outer factors $\Delta A^{-1}$ are the scalar $\Delta_q/x^2$ on $\mathcal H_q$. Thus, after multiplication by $q^2$, the first insertion is at most $2x^{-2}P_qE_pP_q$. We obtain on $\mathcal G$, for a child in its annulus, $$\label{edge:parent-inequality}
 \widehat s_q
 \le Cx^{-2}\mathbf E[\|P_qE_pP_q\|\mid W,\mathcal F_q]
       +C_\gamma e^{-c_1k_p}.$$ Only $\Delta_q$ is inverted outside the covariance in <a href="#edge:transition-covariance" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:transition-covariance">[edge:transition-covariance]</a>; directions with arbitrarily small new parent precision cause no loss.

<a id="edge:compression"></a>
We next compress $E_p$ before imposing $\mathcal G$. The assertion is trivial when $E_p=0$; otherwise $e$ is defined by $\mathcal V_p$. The retained spectral set supplies $ck_p\le\dim\mathcal H_p\le Ck_p$ and $\dim\mathcal H_q\le Cx^3k_p$; after increasing the threshold, $\dim(\mathcal H_p\cap e^\perp)$ is also comparable to $k_p$. Condition under $\mathbf P$ on the spectrum, $W_p$ in physical coordinates, the physical field $h_p$, and its spectral coordinates. Equation <a href="#edge:path-likelihood" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:path-likelihood">[edge:path-likelihood]</a> makes the remaining rotation in $e^\perp\cap\mathcal H_p$ exactly Haar. The operator $E_p$ is fixed under this conditioning: its definition uses only these parent data. For a uniformly rotating unit vector $v$ in this space, the Gaussian representation of the uniform sphere gives $$\mathbf P\left(
 v^{\mathsf T}E_pv>
       \frac{C(\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}E_p+t\|E_p\|)}{k_p}
       \,\middle|\,\text{parent data}\right)
       \le C(e^{-t}+e^{-c_0k_p}).$$ Indeed the numerator is a positive Gaussian quadratic form, and the Gaussian squared norm in the denominator is at least a fixed fraction of the dimension except with $e^{-c_0k_p}$ probability. A fixed-resolution net chosen in the spectral child unit sphere before the remaining Haar rotation has at most $\exp(C\dim\mathcal H_q)\le\exp(Cx^3k_p)$ points. Project each rotated net vector onto $e^\perp$. Conditional on the parent data, it has a fixed norm at most one and a uniformly rotating direction. With $t=C_2x^3k_p$, a sufficiently large $C_2$ pays for the net, and a sufficiently small $\gamma$ pays for the second exponential term. The net estimate for a positive quadratic form gives $$\label{edge:compression}
 \|P_qE_pP_q\|
 \le C\left(\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}E_p}{k_p}+x^3\|E_p\|\right)$$ outside a set of unconditional $\mathbf P$-probability $Ce^{-c_\gamma k_p}$. This is the compression argument of (OpenAI 2026d, Lemma 4.5, Equation (4.6)) <a id="pm-cite-51"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)]; no restriction to $\mathcal G$ was made in the Haar law.

<a id="edge:conditioning-good-event"></a>
Average <a href="#edge:parent-inequality" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:parent-inequality">[edge:parent-inequality]</a> over $I_q=[q/(2\gamma),q/\gamma]$, with normalized logarithmic measure. On $\mathcal G$ outside the failure event in <a href="#edge:frobenius-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:frobenius-bound">[edge:frobenius-bound]</a>, <a href="#edge:tangent-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:tangent-bounds">[edge:tangent-bounds]</a> and Cauchy–Schwarz give $$\operatorname{Av}_{p\in I_q}\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}E_p}{k_p}
       \le C_\gamma k_q^{-b},\qquad b=1/10.$$ Here $\operatorname{Av}$ denotes that normalized logarithmic integral. On its failure the same averaged trace is bounded, because $E_p$ is bounded everywhere and $\dim\mathcal H_p\le Ck_p$. Its contribution on that failure, with $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}$ inserted, has expectation at most $Ce^{-c k_q^{a_1}}$. The failures of <a href="#edge:compression" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:compression">[edge:compression]</a> are charged in the same way by the bounded $\|E_p\|$. These estimates are applied to the whole parent-scale integral before its conditional expectation. For every nonnegative error cost $Y$, $$\label{edge:conditioning-good-event}
 \mathbf E[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\mathbf E(Y\mid W,\mathcal F_q)]
       =\mathbf E[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}Y],$$ because $\mathcal G$ is measurable from $W$.

<a id="edge:curvature-recurrence"></a>
The norm term in <a href="#edge:compression" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:compression">[edge:compression]</a> has coefficient $Cx^{-2}x^3\le C\gamma$. The initial choice of $\gamma$ makes this coefficient $\theta<1/2$. We have proved, on $\mathcal G$, $$\label{edge:curvature-recurrence}
 \begin{split}
 \widehat s_q&\le
 \theta\operatorname{Av}_{p\in I_q}
       \mathbf E[\widehat s_p\mid W,\mathcal F_q]
       +C_\gamma k_q^{-b}+\operatorname{err}_q,\\
 \operatorname{err}_q&\ge0,\qquad
 \mathbf E[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\operatorname{err}_q]
       \le C e^{-c k_q^\beta}
 \end{split}$$ for some $\beta>0$. Off the child annulus the left side is zero. The bounded definition of $E_p$ is essential here: no cost polynomial in $n$ is charged on a failed parent interval.

Use a barrier $B k_q^{-\alpha}$, with $0<\alpha\le b$ and $B$ large. Since $k_p=k_qx^{-3}$, $$\theta\operatorname{Av}_{p\in I_q}B k_p^{-\alpha}
       \le\theta(2\gamma)^{3\alpha}B k_q^{-\alpha}.$$ It absorbs the deterministic error in <a href="#edge:curvature-recurrence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:curvature-recurrence">[edge:curvature-recurrence]</a>. Taking positive parts, applying conditional Jensen, and using <a href="#edge:conditioning-good-event" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:conditioning-good-event">[edge:conditioning-good-event]</a>, we obtain $$A(q):=\mathbf E[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}
       (\widehat s_q-Bk_q^{-\alpha})_+]
 \le\theta\operatorname{Av}_{p\in I_q}A(p)+Ce^{-c k_q^\beta}.$$ For each deterministic nonactivation scale $r_n\le p\le C_\gamma r_n$, use (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 4.2, Equation (4.2)) <a id="pm-cite-52"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] within its stated range. Under the biased law $\mathbf P$, it gives $p^2K_p\preceq(1+C(p^{a_0}+k_p^{-a_0}))I$ outside a set whose intersection with the full event $\mathcal G_n^{\rm FUA}$ has probability at most $Ce^{-n^{\xi_0}}$. Since $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G_n^{\rm FUA}$, the same failure bound holds after intersection with $\mathcal G$. Here $pk_p=np^4\to0$, so $p^{a_0}\le k_p^{-a_0}$, and $k_p\asymp n^{3\cdot10^{-4}}$. By taking $\alpha\le a_0$ and a sufficiently small positive terminal exponential power, the same bound for $A(p)$ is $Ce^{-c k_p^{\beta_0}}$.

Every parent generation multiplies $k$ by at least $\Lambda=(2\gamma)^{-3}>1$. Iteration, including the terminal bound, gives for a suitably decreased $\beta_*>0$ $$A(q)\le C\sum_{j\ge0}\theta^j
       e^{-c(\Lambda^jk_q)^{\beta_*}}
       \le C e^{-c'k_q^{\beta_*}}.$$ Markov’s inequality at the barrier costs only a factor $k_q^\alpha$, absorbed by the exponential. On $\mathcal G$, <a href="#edge:local-parent-validity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:local-parent-validity">[edge:local-parent-validity]</a> holds throughout the full auxiliary annulus, and <a href="#edge:shrinking-annulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:shrinking-annulus">[edge:shrinking-annulus]</a> removes the annulus truncation. Decrease to a common positive exponent in the barrier and probability. This proves <a href="#edge:positive-curvature-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:positive-curvature-bound">[edge:positive-curvature-bound]</a>. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-edge-positive-curvature-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-edge-positive-curvature</summary>

*Proof of Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>.* Lemmas <a href="#edge:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spectral">4</a> and <a href="#edge:norm-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:norm-density">5</a> prove the spectral and saddle assertions. Lemmas <a href="#edge:spherical-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:spherical-tails">6</a>, <a href="#edge:cube-caps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:cube-caps">10</a>, and <a href="#edge:path-annuli" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="edge:path-annuli">11</a> prove the static, curvature, projection, and ordinary annulus assertions. Assign a fixed fraction of the requested failure probability to each of their spectral and disorder restrictions, and take their finite intersection. The length bounds give a deterministic $R_{\rm ann}$ containing the full annulus; include a further cube-cap request for the static comparisons on that ball, retaining the previously chosen width $s_0$. We select one additional event, independent of $f$, for the variance.

In the reduction above take $\eta_p=Ck_p^{-a}$ and let $\mathcal N$ be the jointly measurable field set where $p^2K_p(h)\npreceq(1+Ck_p^{-a})I_{\mathcal H_p}$. Set its indicator to one at activation scales, which have zero scale measure for each $W$. At every deterministic nonactivation scale its evaluation at $h_p$ is the failure event in <a href="#edge:positive-curvature-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:positive-curvature-bound">[edge:positive-curvature-bound]</a>. Use $Z_p$ and the common cost $\rho_p$ from <a href="#edge:common-failure-cost" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:common-failure-cost">[edge:common-failure-cost]</a>; both are independent of $f$.

<a id="edge:weighted-failure"></a>
<a id="edge:quenched-error-intervals"></a>
Under $\mathbf P$, conditional Jensen and the spherical identity give $$\mathbf E[\mu_{p,h_p}(Z_p)^2]
       \le\mathbf E[\mu_{p,h_p}(Z_p^2)]
       =\mathbf E[Z_p^2]\le C,$$ by the uncapped spherical projection tail. Cauchy–Schwarz and <a href="#edge:positive-curvature-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:positive-curvature-bound">[edge:positive-curvature-bound]</a>, absorbing $k_p$ in the exponential, imply $$\label{edge:weighted-failure}
 E_U[L_\circ\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\rho_p]\le C e^{-c k_p^a}.$$ The left side is an ordinary path expectation averaged with the Haar bias. Take $q_j=2^j(K/n)^{1/3}$ up to $r_n$. Fubini, <a href="#edge:weighted-failure" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:weighted-failure">[edge:weighted-failure]</a>, and $L_\circ\ge1/2$ bound the expected ordinary cost on $[q_j,2q_j]$, intersected with $\mathcal G$, by $Ce^{-c k_{q_j}^a}$. Markov and $$\sum_{j\ge0}e^{-c(K8^j)^a}\le C e^{-c'K^a}$$ give an event of arbitrarily large limiting disorder probability on which, simultaneously in $j$, $$\label{edge:quenched-error-intervals}
 \int_{q_j}^{\min\{2q_j,r_n\}}\rho_p\,\mathrm d\log p
       \le C e^{-c k_{q_j}^a}.$$ Increase $K$ and use <a href="#edge:haar-bias" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:haar-bias">[edge:haar-bias]</a> for the single discarded event. This event is independent of $f$.

The conditional-variance estimate of (OpenAI 2026d, Proposition 4.1, Equation (4.1)) <a id="pm-cite-53"></a>[[FUA](#ref-FUA)] holds on an ordinary event of arbitrarily large limiting probability, simultaneously for all real cube functions and scales in its stated interval $[r_n,p_*]$. Its remainder is $Ce^{-n^{\xi_0}}\|f\|_\infty^2$. We use it only at $r_n$, for $0\le f\le1$: $$V_{r_n}(f)\le Cr_n^{-2}\mathcal E(f)+Ce^{-n^{\xi_0}}.$$ Intersect this event with the preceding ones. In <a href="#edge:variance-amplification" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:variance-amplification">[edge:variance-amplification]</a> with terminal scale $r_n$, its amplified energy is $Cp^{-2}\mathcal E(f)$. Its amplified remainder is bounded by $Ce^{-c k_p^a}$ after decreasing $a>0$, since $k_p\le k_{r_n}=n^{3\cdot10^{-4}}$. For the other errors use <a href="#edge:quenched-error-intervals" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:quenched-error-intervals">[edge:quenched-error-intervals]</a>. The first partial dyadic interval has $k_{q_j}\asymp k_p$; the rest increase geometrically. Hence $$\sum_{q_j\gtrsim p}C(q_j/p)^2e^{-c k_{q_j}^a}
       \le C e^{-c'k_p^a}.$$ Applying <a href="#edge:variance-amplification" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:variance-amplification">[edge:variance-amplification]</a> proves the first inequality of <a href="#edge:variance-estimates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:variance-estimates">[edge:variance-estimates]</a>. It extends to activation points by continuity of $V_p$ in $B_p$.

For the second inequality impose the additional fixed annulus estimate with $\zeta_*=\min\{\zeta,s_0/2\}$. On that annulus the coarse covariance and <a href="#edge:gradient-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:gradient-bounds">[edge:gradient-bounds]</a> contribute $CV_p$. For its complement, Cauchy–Schwarz and conditional Jensen give $$\begin{split}
 k_pQ_\mu[\mathbf 1_{\{|\alpha_p(h_p)|>\zeta_* p^2\}}\mu_{p,h_p}(Z_p)]
 &\le k_pQ_\mu\{|\alpha_p(h_p)|>\zeta_* p^2\}^{1/2}
       \mu(Z_p^2)^{1/2}\\
 &\le C e^{-c k_p}.
\end{split}$$ Here $\mu(Z_p^2)\le C$ holds at every scale on the chosen uncapped cube projection event, and the ordinary annulus estimate is also simultaneous in scale. Weakening the exponent if needed proves the second inequality of <a href="#edge:variance-estimates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="edge:variance-estimates">[edge:variance-estimates]</a>, on the same event for every $f$. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:warming"></a>
### Warming at the critical time scale

The first step toward a quench limit is to control the finite law after any positive multiple of $T_n=n^{2/3}$, uniformly in its initial distribution. The edge estimates of Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a> give the required control at the smallest observation scales. We turn them into dissipation estimates by measuring how much relative entropy survives between two observations. Larger entropy levels are treated by the observation path to a product measure from (OpenAI 2026b, sec. 19) <a id="pm-cite-54"></a>[[CM](#ref-CM)].

For a probability $\rho$ on the cube, write $$w_s^\rho=\frac{\,\mathrm d(\rho P_{sT_n})}{\,\mathrm d\mu},\qquad s\ge0.$$ Thus $w_s=w_s^{\nu_n}$ for the uniform initial law used elsewhere in the paper. Write $$p_t(\sigma,\tau)=\frac{P_t(\sigma,\tau)}{\mu(\tau)}$$ for the heat kernel relative to $\mu$. We use $\log_+z=\max\{\log z,0\}$ for $z>0$, with $z(\log_+z)^m=0$ at $z=0$. For a probability $\pi$ and a nonnegative integrable function $z$, write $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\pi(z)=\pi[z\log z]-\pi[z]\log\pi[z],$$ with $0\log0=0$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\pi(0)=0$. For a probability $\nu\ll\pi$, let $D(\nu\Vert\pi)=\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\pi(\,\mathrm d\nu/\,\mathrm d\pi)$, and set this relative entropy to $+\infty$ otherwise.

<a id="stmt-thm-warming"></a>
<div id="thm:warming" class="theorem">

<a id="warm:entropy"></a>
<a id="warm:kernel"></a>
<a id="warm:log-moment"></a>
**Theorem 15** (Warming from arbitrary initial laws). *Suppose that the couplings are Gaussian. Fix $\vartheta>0$, an integer $m\ge1$, and $0<\xi<1/100$. There are measurable disorder events $\mathcal G_n$, a constant $C<\infty$, and deterministic $\varepsilon_n\downarrow0$ such that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(\mathcal G_n)\ge1-\vartheta$, and the following inequalities hold on $\mathcal G_n$, for all sufficiently large $n$. The constant is independent of the initial law $\rho$, which may be chosen after the disorder. $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\mu(w_s^\rho)&\le C(1+s^{-1.54}),
       &&s>0,\quad\hbox{for every probability }\rho ,
       \label{warm:entropy}\\
 \|P_{sT_n}\|_{L^1(\mu)\to L^\infty(\mu)}
       &=\max_{\sigma,\tau}p_{sT_n}(\sigma,\tau)
       \le C\exp(C s^{-1.54}),
       &&s\ge\varepsilon_n ,
       \label{warm:kernel}\\
 \left(1+\mu\!\left[
       w_s^\rho(\log_+w_s^\rho)^m\right]\right)^{1/m}
       &\le C\left(1+s^{-1/(2/3-\xi)}\right),
       &&s>0,\quad\hbox{for every probability }\rho .
       \label{warm:log-moment}
\end{aligned}$$ The events and constants may depend on the displayed fixed parameters. In particular the order $m$ is fixed before $n$ tends to infinity.*

</div>

The distinction between <a href="#warm:entropy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="warm:entropy">[warm:entropy]</a> and <a href="#warm:kernel" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="warm:kernel">[warm:kernel]</a> is useful. Entropy is controlled at every positive time; the stronger kernel estimate begins at a deterministic time tending to zero in the rescaled units. The log-moment estimate supplies a different form of control at the very short times used later in the replacement argument.

<a id="warm:profile-section"></a>
#### A restricted dissipation profile

<a id="warm:modified-classical"></a>
Recall $\mathcal I(z)=\mathcal E(z,\log z)$, with the extended value at zeros. On a two-point edge, the inequality $$(a^2-b^2)(\log a^2-\log b^2)\ge4(a-b)^2,\qquad a,b>0,$$ follows by integrating $1/u$ between $a$ and $b$ and applying Cauchy–Schwarz. Summing it in the reversible edge representation gives $$\mathcal I(f^2)\ge4\mathcal E(f).                                      \label{warm:modified-classical}$$ The inequality extends to nonnegative $f$ by decreasing positive regularization.

The next profile concerns a bounded function whose square tilt retains a definite fraction of the logarithm of its inverse mass. All its inequalities hold simultaneously in the function.

<a id="stmt-warm-profiles"></a>
<div id="warm:profiles" class="proposition">

<a id="warm:restricted-class"></a>
<a id="warm:modified-profile"></a>
<a id="warm:classical-profile"></a>
**Proposition 16** (Restricted dissipation profiles). *Fix $C_{\mathrm{lev}}<\infty$ and $0<\xi<1/100$. With tight constants, there are a threshold $K_0<\infty$ and a number $\delta>0$ such that every $0\le f\le1$ satisfying $$N=\mu[f^2]=e^{-L},\qquad
 K_0\le L\le C_{\mathrm{lev}} n,\qquad
 D\!\left(\frac{f^2\mu}{N}\middle\Vert\mu\right)\ge\frac L2
                                                               \label{warm:restricted-class}$$ obeys $$\begin{aligned}
 T_n\,\frac{\mathcal I(f^2)}{N}&\ge c_\xi L^{5/3-\xi},
                                                               \label{warm:modified-profile}\\
 T_n\,\frac{\mathcal E(f)}{N}&\ge c
 \begin{cases}
 L^{1.662},&L\le n^\delta,\\
 L^{1.162},&L>n^\delta .
 \end{cases}                                                   \label{warm:classical-profile}
\end{aligned}$$ Here a threshold, a positive exponent, and constants are tight in the following precise sense. For each $\vartheta>0$ they can be fixed, independently of $f$, on disorder events of limiting lower probability at least $1-\vartheta$. They may depend on $C_{\mathrm{lev}},\xi,\vartheta$.*

</div>

The modified profile yields entropy dissipation and the higher logarithmic moments after the reduction by level sets. The classical profile yields a support profile and hence the heat kernel bound. We prove the profiles in three ranges: $L\le n^\delta$ by the argument with two observations; $n^\delta<L\le\lambda n$ by the proportional branch of the source path; and $\lambda n\le L\le C_{\mathrm{lev}}n$ by the product endpoint and the estimate for a reweighted mean below, for a small fixed $\lambda$ chosen later.

<a id="stmt-warm-small-profile"></a>
<div id="warm:small-profile" class="lemma">

<a id="warm:small-profile-bound"></a>
**Lemma 17** (Entropy between two observation scales). *Fix $C_{\mathrm{lev}}<\infty$. For every fixed $\kappa>0$, there are tight $K_0$ and $\delta>0$ such that every $f$ satisfying <a href="#warm:restricted-class" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="warm:restricted-class">[warm:restricted-class]</a> with $L\le n^\delta$ satisfies $$T_n\,\frac{\mathcal E(f)}{N}\ge c_\kappa L^{5/3-\kappa}.
                                                               \label{warm:small-profile-bound}$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-warm-small-profile"><summary>Proof of stmt-warm-small-profile</summary>

*Proof.* Fix first one instance of Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>, with $\epsilon_{\rm sp}\le1$, $K\ge1$, and a variance-remainder exponent $0<a\le1$, decreasing the exponent if necessary. Its constants are fixed on a disorder event of arbitrarily high limiting probability. Choose $M>1$ sufficiently large that $$Ma>1,\qquad \frac{2M}{3}>\frac53-\kappa .$$ We retain this variance estimate when imposing further cap tolerances below; intersection with finitely many additional events does not change its already chosen exponent $a$. Choose $\delta>0$ so small that $M\delta/3<10^{-4}$. This leaves every fixed factor buffer about the scales below within $r_n=n^{-1/3+10^{-4}}$ for large $n$. Use the same fixed small $\gamma>0$ as in the covariance iteration of Section <a href="#sec:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:edge-estimates">3</a>. Choose the bridge tolerance $\epsilon>0$ after $M$, with $2(M-1)\epsilon/3<\kappa$.

<a id="warm:small-variance"></a>
For a small fixed $c_0>0$, to be chosen using only the projection-tail constants, define $$k_{p_1}=np_1^3=c_0L,\qquad k_R=nR^3=L^M.$$ Increasing $K_0$ puts these scales above the threshold of Proposition <a href="#prop:edge-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:edge-estimates">3</a>. Suppose, for a contradiction, that $T_n\mathcal E(f)/N<L^{5/3-\kappa}$. If $F_R(h)=\mu_{R,h}[f]$ and $V_R=Q_\mu[\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(f\mid h_R)]$, that proposition gives $$\frac{V_R}{N}
 \le C L^{5/3-\kappa-2M/3}
       +C\exp\{L-cL^{Ma}\}=o_{K_0\to\infty}(1).
                                                               \label{warm:small-variance}$$ The estimate is uniform in $n,L,f$ in the present range, because $R^2T_n=L^{2M/3}$.

<a id="warm:residual-observation-entropy"></a>
<a id="warm:entropy-continuity"></a>
Consider the joint ordinary law $Q_\mu$ of the spin and its observation path through $R$. Change this law to $Q_{\rm spin}$ or $Q_{\rm obs}$ by the respective densities $$\Lambda^{\rm spin}=\frac{f^2}{N},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^{\rm obs}=\frac{F_R(h_R)^2}{A},
 \qquad
 A=Q_\mu[F_R^2]=N-V_R .$$ For $K_0$ large, $A\ge N/2$, so both densities are at most $2e^L$. For any of these laws, $Q|_p$ denotes restriction to $\sigma(h_q:0\le q\le p)$, always excluding the spin. Define, for $p<R$, $$\label{warm:residual-observation-entropy}
 H(p)=D(Q_{\rm obs}\Vert Q_\mu)
       -D(Q_{\rm obs}|_p\Vert Q_\mu|_p).$$ The first entropy is on the full joint law. Since its likelihood is measurable from $h_R$, it equals the relative entropy on the terminal observation sigma-field. Both terms are finite by the likelihood bound, and the conditional entropy chain rule identifies $H(p)$ with the expected entropy of the terminal observation tilt remaining after the prefix through $p$. To compare the two tilts, note that $Q_\mu[fF_R]=A$, and hence $$Q_\mu\left[\left(\frac f{\sqrt N}
                  -\frac{F_R}{\sqrt A}\right)^2\right]
 =2\left(1-\sqrt{\frac AN}\right)\le\frac{2V_R}{N}.$$ Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the $L^1(Q_\mu)$ distance between the two densities by $2\sqrt{2V_R/N}$. This bound persists after projection to any part of the observation path. If two projected densities $u,v\le2e^L$ have $L^1$ distance $d$, then $$\left|Q_\mu[u\log u]-Q_\mu[v\log v]\right|
 \le (1+L+\log2)d+C.                                      \label{warm:entropy-continuity}$$ Indeed $x\log x$ has derivative bounded by $1+L+\log2$ on $[1,2e^L]$, while its absolute value is bounded on $[0,1]$. It follows from <a href="#warm:small-variance" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="warm:small-variance">[warm:small-variance]</a> that the two relative entropies, both before and after any projection, differ by $o(L)$, uniformly as $K_0$ increases.

We bound the information revealed at $p_1$ under the spin tilt. The field $h_{p_1}$ is a sufficient statistic for the path through that scale. Let $Q_0$ be the output of the same Gaussian channel with zero signal. Convexity of relative entropy and evenness of $\mu$ give $$D(Q_{\rm spin}|_{p_1}\Vert Q_0)
